#4018. 2027 Video Game Grammy Nominations Include Avatar: Frontiers Of Pandora For The Third Time

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

#4017. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#4016. Make Room For GTAVI By Deleting Your PS5 Trophy Clips

Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.

You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.

Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.

First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button.

Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips.

After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again.

In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.

#4015. Hardware Review: Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited - Solid Xbox-Style PS5 Controller Undercuts Its Competition

For the last month, I’ve been levelling up my game with the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited, a hefty pro controller for PS5. With a myriad of customisable features, including trigger travel length and even its weight, I’m going to break down whether this controller is worth your time.

The NACON Revolution 5 Unlimited is a big old pro controller, compatible with both PS5 and PC. It connects to PS5 via a dongle, can also connect wirelessly, offering 2.4Ghz connection for either, and offers Bluetooth connectivity too.

It features TMR thumbsticks, eradicating the worry of stick drift, along with swappable thumbstick tips and varying weights to fit in the grips of the controller, so you can customise the feel of the controller to your liking.

The big headliner here is a screen display in the centre of the controller, which allows access to simple customising menus without the need for an additional app — but we'll get into that later.

This Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited will set you back £179.90/$229.90, actually making it one of the cheaper options in the pro controller market.

The NACON Revolution 5 Unlimited, which I’m just going to call the Rev5 from now on, comes in a rugged, hardshell case, with NACON branding embossed on the front.

Inside, the controller, of course, along with a collection of switchable thumbsticks, a D-Pad alternative, and weights which can be placed on the inside of the controller, a braided USB-A to C cable, the dongle, and the charging base.

The form factor is easily one of my favourite things about the Rev5. This is a pretty large, meaty controller, which, personally, I really like. It fills the hands, and immediately, all of the buttons feel like they are in naturally reachable places – something that wasn’t the case with the SCUF Omega, in my opinion.

Your eye will immediately be drawn to this little screen in the middle, and we’ll get to some of its features in a minute, but it definitely gives the Rev5 a premium look. The grips of the controller offer a ribbed rubber coating with a sleek black finish. The thumbsticks, d-pad, and triggers all have textured finishes, giving each a nice firm feel. There’s a satisfying clicky feel to the face buttons and back paddles, which are naturally placed where my fingers wrap around the back of the controller.

I love the triggers on this thing, which remind me of the Xbox controllers, actually. They have a nice smooth travel for the longer setting, but can also be switched to a mouse-like click, with a toggle on the back. I have to say, these are some of my favourite trigger length toggles that I’ve used on a pro controller. They are so easy to access and customise, without the need for longer nails to pick at them.

My only real complaints about the design are that the finish does make the controller a victim to smudges and smears, and the substitute button for the touchpad is a little small, which can be a pain if you want to quickly check leaderboards, for example.

Connecting this thing to the PS5 is a right doddle. You can use it wired with the braided cable, but most of my use was with the dongle.

What I really liked about this dongle is that it could be used whilst plugged into the back of the charging base, with a USB-A to C cable connecting to the PS5, meaning you can connect and charge the Rev5 with the use of just one USB-A port. However, if you're on the go, you can also just plug the dongle straight into the PS5, without the need for the charging base.

Annoyingly, however, you aren’t able to turn the PS5 on with this controller. You have to manually turn it on, then connect the Rev5, regardless of whether you are connecting wirelessly or wired.

Then there is that screen, which is really cool, but it did take me a moment to get my head around. A customise button on the top of the controller halts all inputs to the console and lets you navigate a simple menu system.

Here you can customise things like thumbstick dead zones, audio and mic input (if you’re using a wired headset), and customise each of the six additional buttons around the controller.

You’re then able to make four custom profiles, which you can switch between with a tap of the Profile button on the back of the controller. It’s not quite DualSense Edge levels of ease, but it is great.

If a little screen menu isn’t cutting it for you, there is also still the option to download the Nacon app and customise more intensely from there.

Then there is the physical customisation. You are able to switch out thumbsticks, the D-pad, and apply additional weights in the grips of the controllers. All of this is incredibly accessible, as there are no tools required. You can just pull one thing off and replace it with another. The only thing I had a bit of struggle getting off was the smaller variation of the d-pad.

Honestly, I think the Rev5 feels great. Once you have a profile that suits you, this thing is just moulded to the hand, with each of its additional paddles easily within reach, and its physical customisation options making it feel tailor-made to you.

I love the travel of the trigger if going for long triggers, but it features a really satisfying mouse-click if you customise it to short triggers too. The TMR sticks do have that weightless feel that's typical for thumbstick utilising Hall Effect tech, but I adjusted to it quite quickly.

The easy profile swapping and customisation on the actual controller, and the feel in the hand, meant I was more inclined than ever to just use this thing for regular games, not just those competitive titles like The Finals or Modern Warfare 4. I actually played most of Zero Parades using this controller, just because it was comfortable to use, despite not using a single customisation aspect.

There is a pretty big flaw, however, regarding that screen – the lack of a touchpad. The button initially used to replace it is very small and not as easy to touch as I’d like when opening up maps or menus in-game. Of course, you can just use one of the other shortcuts for this if you’re so inclined.

However, it does mean if there ever is a game that utilises the touchpad, like Ghost of Yotei, for example, you’re kind of out of luck. Admittedly, there isn’t a huge number of games that utilise this feature, or have anything beyond a single-use touch, so most of the time, it’s a bit of a non-issue. However, it is something to consider if this is to be your main controller.

As is the case with these controllers – and the same with the last Nacon controller I reviewed – this thing doesn’t feature rumble on the PS5, meaning it’s severely lacking in the immersive department.

For a lot of people, that’s just not going to matter, but for me it’s an additional feature that always brings me back to the DualSense Edge – a pro controller with full haptics and adaptive triggers. What’s even worse is that there is actually a rumble motor in this controller, but it’s limited to use on PC.

I can’t knock the controller too much for that because outside of the DualSense Edge, most pro controllers won't feature any form of rumble. It’s just a shame because, for me, if it had rumble on PS5, it would be among my favourite controllers.

Despite my musing over a lack of rumble support on PS5, I do think the Rev5 is worth considering if you’re in the market for a pro controller.

It feels fantastic in the hand, with a satisfying click and travel to each of its buttons; the customisation is easy to change from a software perspective, but also incredibly accessible from a hardware perspective.

It features great build quality, the charger/dongle system is handy, and it comes with a pretty cool carry case. And you get all of this for about £20 to £30 less than most other pro controllers.

Is it perfect? No way. But it’s a pretty damn nice controller.

Swearing an oath of loyalty to PlayStation with the arrival of the PS4, our resident video-maker and Irn-Bru loving Scot prides himself as an expert in modern-day Sony. However, eight playthroughs of The Last Of Us later, and no Platinum to show for it, will forever be his greatest shame.

#4014. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#4013. Guide: 42 Switch 1 & 2 Games You Should Check Out In Nintendo's Black Friday eShop Sale (Europe)

Every game we scored 9/10 or higher, plus a personal pick

The once one-day event of 'Black Friday' seems to last for almost all of November these days. Anyway, Nintendo has kicked off its digital discounts with an eShop sale in Europe.

The EU Black Friday eShop sale is now live and will be sticking around until 29th November, offering big savings on a bunch of Switch 1 and 2 bangers.

We have assembled the following list to highlight the cream of the crop — who has time to scroll through thousands of games, after all. Below, you'll find every game in Nintendo's Black Friday sale that we awarded a 9/10 or higher. We've also added a personal pick at the end from the games that fall below that threshold, because we just couldn't resist.

As ever, if you're looking to grab some eShop credit before diving in, we've got you covered with the following links from our store.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim is a wonderful achievement for dynamic storytelling, as it puts forth a compelling and multifaceted narrative that’ll keep you guessing right up until the very end.

This excellent story, combined with enjoyable combat portions, a striking art style, and some top-notch voice acting make for an experience that you shouldn't miss. It’s the kind of game that’ll have you wishing that you could play it again for the first time, just so all its best elements could be new again.

Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown is the absolute pinnacle of the series and despite coming to Switch over five years after other platforms, this 'impossible' Switch conversion does very little to degrade the experience. Long-time franchise players and military aviation enthusiasts will be overwhelmed by the fan service at every turn, from craters on the ground to airplanes, liveries, callsigns, and emblems shouting out to previous entries.

We understand the genre is uniquely niche, but if this is your first foray into the franchise, this conversion is a perfect gateway into this rich, revered series. You get tons of content and an epic single-player campaign wrapped up in triple-A presentation that delivers the most comprehensive portable experience ever from Project Aces.

Aegis Defenders is a fantastic game, brilliantly blending the tower defence and platforming genres in a unique way to produce a memorable and enjoyable experience.

Lovable characters, interesting lore, plenty of secrets, engaging gameplay, and gorgeous presentation combine to make this a must-have for your Switch, a real gem on the eShop.

AI: The Somnium Files – nirvanA Initiative is one of the most interesting visual novels we’ve played through in a while. The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.

Even with some minor control issues, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.

Alwa’s Legacy is an excellent example of how to do a proper sequel; it takes everything that Alwa's Awakening did well and builds on it, adds in a few new ideas of its own, and corrects the issues that were previously present.

It may be a little on the short side, but Alwa’s Legacy is the special sort of game that only comes around once in a great while, reminding you of the kind of quality that’s possible when a dedicated crew puts in the time to make a polished and tightly designed final product.

While this turn-based affair might look, move, and feel just like a real board game, Armello is actually a completely original creation — and one that does more than simply doff its cap at the world of tabletop gaming. From the deep tactics of its living board game gameplay to the sheer charm of its worldbuilding and animal character designs, it's a quest filled with back-stabbing, political power plays, and rampaging monsters that’s different each and every time you play. It’s at its absolute best when played in multiplayer, that human factor making for an even more unpredictable battle for the corrupted throne. The Switch version has had its ups and downs since launch, with some updates making things worse, but it's apparently back to being in a playable state on Nintendo's console. As such, you’d be doing yourself a disservice not to add this anthropomorphic tale to your wishlist.

Astral Ascent is a prime example of a game that amounts to more than the sum of its parts. Its strong character design, hi-bit visuals, tight combat, memorable bosses, and broad build variety have all featured in games you’ve probably played before—there’s nothing ‘new’ here.

But to write it off as just 'another one of those' in a crowded genre would be to miss out on one of the most delightful and surprising releases of 2023. Astral Ascent is comfortably one of the best roguelites available on the Switch. Don't miss it.

Catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent new character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.

If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough new content here to make it worth diving in all over again.

An extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface issues which are easily ignored.

At roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.

It's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.

There isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.

Even so many years after its 2005 debut, Devil May Cry 3 remains one of the very best action games ever made. It may have aged in places, but that turbo-charged, combo-heavy action feels as fresh today as it did back in the mid-noughties.

The new Freestyle mode – which lets players swap combat styles on the fly at any point during the action – is a genuinely excellent addition to the package, and the ability to play Bloody Palace in local co-op is the cherry on top of a Switch port that should appeal to anyone interested in sampling the devilish delights of this all-time classic.

Dragon Ball FighterZ on the Switch is, simply put, one of the best fighting games we've seen on the system. Arc System Works went the extra mile in capturing the essence of the source material and distilled it into an incredible brawler that has lost nothing in the transition to Nintendo's hybrid console.

The stunning visuals, intense action, and easy-to-master controls make FighterZ a game all fans of the genre should have in their library. If you only play this kind of game casually, it remains a must-own.

Every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first place. Forager features wonderfully designed crafting mechanics, addictive progression systems and more charm than you can possibly handle. Although it has very minor drawbacks, there's enough good stuff present here for us to confidently recommend adding Forager to your collection.

Heretic + Hexen is yet another slam dunk for Nightdive Studios. This new release revamps both titles with modern controls, bonus content, and thoughtful changes to the core design that make each game a delight to play.

Granted, these are still FPS titles from the mid-'90s, so your mileage will definitely vary, but for returning fans and those with a particular fondness for old-school 'boomer shooters', you really can't go wrong. Now let's get a native Switch 2 port with 120fps please, Nightdive.

An absolute pleasure from start to finish, what Kaze and the Wild Masks lacks in originality it makes up for in the strength of its level design, responsive controls, kinetic move set and attractive visuals. Excellent, action-packed platforming through and through, with great gameplay variety and gimmicks that don’t compromise on what the game is best at — challenging, fast-paced obstacle courses and deviously hidden secret areas.

Easiest sell? Kaze and the Wild Masks is to Donkey Kong Country what Freedom Planet was to Sonic the Hedgehog. Don’t miss this one.

It may be over in the blink of an eye, but Kraino Origins proves itself to be a well-crafted and deeply enjoyable old-school action platformer while it lasts. There’s a little bit of Mega Man in here, a little more Castlevania, some Super Mario Bros. 3, but Kraino doesn’t feel overly derivative of such titles, largely because of its excellent level design. With some excellent 8-bit pixel art, this is an affordable and brief entry in the neo-retro genre, and one that we would definitely recommend.

The original La-Mulana was a masterpiece in its own right, but we’d contend that it’s been edged out by the sequel. What we have here is an expertly-paced, crushingly difficult, and utterly mystifying adventure that constantly beckons you to explore deeper and acquaint yourself with its unique charms. La-Mulana 2 definitely isn’t for everybody – if you consider yourself an impatient or clumsy player, steer clear – but those who put in the time and effort to crack this nut will be deeply satisfied that they did so. We’d give La-Mulana 2 a high recommendation for anybody looking for a deep and challenging new Metroidvania for their Switch; it’s an acquired taste, but one you will come to savour.

Mega Man X Legacy Collection is a fantastic re-release of several must-play gaming classics, presenting them as authentically as possible while still including a few modern features on top that help to improve the overall experience and keep it from feeling antiquated.

Throw in the new X Challenge mode and an enormous archive of museum content and this stands as the definitive way to play the Mega Man X games in the modern era. Four fantastic games, a bevvy of extra content, and the ability to play at home or on the go — nothing not to like here.

Mega Man Zero/ZX Legacy Collection is everything that you could’ve hoped it to be. This is ultimately six great Mega Man games presented to you with a slew of customisable features, extra content, and quality-of-life updates.

If you’re a fan of either Mega Man or side-scrolling action games in general, you owe it to yourself to give this release a go and see what all the fuss is about. These are hard and occasionally frustrating games, but they offer up some rewarding, action-heavy gameplay that even today stands among the best of its class. Don’t pass this collection up.

Monster Hunter Generations Ultimate may lack the accessibility that made Monster Hunter: World such a smash hit, but it more than makes up for it by being a sort of ‘greatest hits’ collection of the high points of the series, giving you hundreds of hours of content to play through. Couple this with the HD visuals, easy-to-use multiplayer, and the ability to play the full experience on the go, and you’ve got a game that will appeal to both veterans and newcomers alike.

It may not necessarily represent the future of the series, but this is a fantastic experience in its own right and a worthy follow-up to the 3DS original, and one that no Switch owner will want to be without, even if series newcomers might want to start with Rise first.

Okami HD is an utterly fantastic piece of software, and we feel you’d be doing yourself a disservice to pass on it. It's a 40-hour adventure that emulates Zelda wonderfully, adds in plenty of memorable mechanics, features one of the most beautiful art styles in gaming, and is completely playable on the go, to boot.

It may be showing its age a bit visually and its combat is sometimes a little on the easy side, but Okami is an important, fun, and notable landmark in gaming history — and one of the easiest recommendations we can make for your Switch library.

Orbitals set out to do something very specific: deliver an action-packed co-operative game while building a new world inspired by anime classics. On those two notes, it smashes it out of the park. The puzzles not only last just the right amount of time, but we were consistently delighted by the clever ways the strict set of tools were utilised, and the many fun ways you interact with this fantastically realised anime world.

Our main complaint is that we wanted much more of it, and while the gameplay itself feels perfectly paced, the somewhat abrupt ending left us wishing more time was spent establishing the stakes and motivations of the story.

Ultimately, Orbitals is a truly phenomenal co-operative title and one of the best ways to spend an evening with a friend this year. With phenomenal visuals, thrilling mechanics, and the brilliant characters and story, this is the new high bar for co-op games.

#4012. Star Wars: Galactic Racer Gets Local Splitscreen Multiplayer Next Year

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been one of 2026’s breakout titles, but much of the game’s praise stems from its exceptional roguelike single-player mode. If you want to race against human players, you can only do so online. Thankfully, for fans of couch multiplayer, that’s going to change.

Developer Fuse Games announced yesterday that local splitscreen multiplayer is coming to Star Wars: Galactic Racer early next year. The mode lets you race up to three other players on the same screen. That's pretty much all there is to it, but given that local multiplayer was the game's biggest omission and, as a result, the most requested addition, there's probably no better news for Galactic Racer fans.

We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027. A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to develop a new mode: Free Play. Choose your vehicle, character, planet, and track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local splitscreen action.[image or embed]

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC. Read our review of the game here.

#4010. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

#4009. The Blood Of Dawnwalker Just Got A Free 1.2 Update, Adding New Game Plus

The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the year's biggest, most ambitious games, and the developers over at Rebel Wolves have done a good job cleaning up bugs and performance issues in the weeks since launch. Today, that trend continued; the new 1.2 update is out now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and it adds New Game Plus.

The new mode is uniquely ideal for a game like Dawnwalker. The narrative is very player-driven, whether it has to do with your literal dialogue options, your ability to manage your vampiric hunger, or the order you complete quests, and all of these elements can cause your experience to vary wildly. It makes sense, then, that players would want to jump back in to try things again and see what might happen if the game is played differently, and New Game Plus allows them to do that while keeping combat fresh.

According to the update notes on the Dawnwalker website, "NG+ unlocks after you complete the game’s Epilogue and lets you experience the story again while keeping your progress – mainly your character level, skills, and inventory." You don't gain access to these skills until you complete the prologue, however, which marks the adventure's proper start.

The new mode will also rebalance the world's level scaling. In the base game, certain areas are much harder than others, but in New Game Plus, all enemies will rise in power to match your level, meaning you can explore the world in whatever order you want. On that note, the level cap has also been raised to 100, and protagonist Coen can collect new, more powerful versions of weapons marked with an "NG+" label.

That's basically everything in this update. Rebel Wolves also added some slight tweaks to combat in the base game and adjusted some geometry in the open world, but the main focus here was New Game Plus. This is in contrast to the 1.1 update, which added a much wider suite of bug fixes and made the game run more smoothly.

#4008. Blizzard will talk about Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred one last time before the expansion's launch next week

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#4007. UK's Health Service Issues Warning Over GTA 6, Urges Players to Take Care of Their Hands

GTA 6 is so massive that even the UK's National Health Service — commonly known as the NHS — has gotten in on the act.

To be fair, the NHS raises a good point with regards to the open world game's imminent release. On Instagram, it's urging players to take regular breaks in order to avoid issues like repetitive strain injury — or RSI for short.

In a cruel twist, the official account's admin has actually had to undergo surgery to fix their problem, meaning that playing GTA 6 at launch is going to be difficult.

"Thoughts and prayers for your admin. Bit of surgery to remove a lump. Great NHS service, bad timing," the post reads.

"Planning on dedicating time to gaming later this week? Try and take regular breaks, obviously. And be mindful of RSI," it continues.

In this case, RSI is caused by overuse of certain muscles in the hands and fingers, brought about by repeated actions. It's a pretty common injury amongst gamers, and without wanting to scare you off completely, it can lead to lasting damage if you refuse to properly rest the impacted area.

The NHS has got a whole page on RSI if you want more information.

Have you ever had an RSI? Remember to pause your game in the comments section below.

#4005. GTA 6 Ties With Zelda: Ocarina Of Time As The Highest-Rated Game Ever

Well folks, it's official: Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews are out, and it's currently tied with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (N64) as the highest-rated game ever on Metacritic.

There may yet be time for things to change as more reviews trickle in, but at the time of writing, GTA 6 is sitting at a remarkable 99 on the aggregate website, based on a total of 134 reviews.

Ocarina of Time, meanwhile, has a mere 22 critic reviews making up that lofty 99 average (it was a different time, man), so one could argue that GTA 6's result is probably more impressive – especially in an age in which it's getting harder and harder to make such an impact.

Our pals over at Push Square were emphatic in their praise, calling GTA 6 "the greatest open world game" in their 10/10 review. Meanwhile, our other pals over at Pure Xbox also gave it 10/10, stating "Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come".

There are 10s all over the damn place, with the only outliers awarding it 9s or 90s at the lowest. It's pretty unprecedented stuff.

We'll keep an eye on things and update this article if GTA 6 does happen to slip below Ocarina of Time. Elsewhere, the latter's Switch 2 remake also released to almost universal acclaim earlier this month. Critic reviews on Metacritic average out at 96, while it also boasts the highest user review score of all time at 9.6.

Also people need to get it out of their heads that journalists are directly paid for good reviews, that's not how it works and they will get you on that every time. It's more like symbiosis- access media is the algae growing on the coral that is the wider industry. They benefit from the continued financial success of AAA games, because early access makes them relevant, and they can monetize that relevance. They have no good reason to ever tear into a bad game (not saying GTA is that, I mean in general) and potentially risk losing access to that company's future works, or worst case scenario, suffer an industry wide blacklist. So they don't, and that's why most games you see from major studios never get scores lower than a 7. Life becomes much simpler when you see the clubhouses for what they are, and understand that you were never invited.

#4004. The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

The Sims 4's Marketplace and user-created content have officially arrived on consoles, a little over a month after their debut on PC.

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

#4003. Review: GTA 6 (Xbox) - The Most Breathtaking Open-World Game Of All Time

This is going to dominate your life for months!

Where do you even start with a game like GTA 6? Not only is it the most highly-anticipated video game we've ever seen, but it's also attempting to live up to ridiculous expectations set by its predecessors over the years. GTA 3 revolutionised how we thought about 3D open-world epics, Vice City and San Andreas pushed things to the next level, GTA 4 took yet another massive step into the HD era, and GTA 5 propelled the series into another stratosphere.

We've all spent the last 13 years trying to figure out what GTA 6 might look like by the time it arrives, and the answer is perhaps more simplistic than some had theorised - it's basically GTA 5 mixed with Red Dead Redemption 2, but with a ton of added detail and ambition on top. That's all it needed to be, and I reckon people are going to absolutely love it.

Before we get to the open world, which is surely the most incredible aspect of the entire game, we should first touch on the story of Lucia and Jason. These two amateur criminals accidentally run into each other and establish a relationship (which can alter between platonic and romantic depending on how you interact throughout the campaign), and after a simple score goes wrong, they find themselves being dragged into more and more dangerous scenarios. That's the basic premise, and the rest is up for you to discover yourself.

The GTA 6 Extended Preview from a few months ago left me very concerned about whether there was enough intrigue to the two main characters (along with the NPCs for that matter), but I needn't have worried. Lucia is a fiesty, hot-headed personality - the type of person who thinks less about the consequences and more about the high life she's determined to acquire - while Jason is extremely laid back to a hilarious extent at times, although also highly capable in pretty much any situation he finds himself in. The two bounce off each other really nicely, and their dynamic definitely remains engaging throughout the campaign's duration.

While I really don't want to spoil anything story-related, the mission structure is very much what you'd expect from GTA 5 and RDR2. In other words, there's a well-balanced mix of laid-back and humorous missions along with more intense shootouts and getaways that significantly ramp up in intensity. They've managed to get really inventive and ambitious with some of the later missions in particular, and I think there's no doubt they're the best of any GTA game.

I also want to point out the use of music in GTA 6's missions, which caught me off-guard and became one of my low-key favourite features. In a nutshell, if you find yourself in the likes of a shootout or a getaway, you'll often notice that curated tunes play in the background to amplify the situation. The developers sometimes even go a step further by making the lighting around you pulsate to the beat, or by introducing lyricists to create a menacing vibe, and it can turn an otherwise generic mission into an amazing one. Seriously, I can't overstate how much I love this feature.

The story itself takes 40ish hours if you completely rush it (which admittedly I've been doing for the most part to hit this embargo), but if you take your time and do at least a decent amount of the optional stuff, it's likely more around 60-100+ hours. As I say, I've enjoyed all of those hours, and I think the campaign seriously hits its stride in the final third - the vast majority of memorable moments are saved for the latter stages.

I don't want you to fixate on the 40-100+ hour figure though, and that's because GTA 6's open world is so incredible and so vast that you could be playing it for months, and likely years, and not see everything it has to offer. We've never seen a GTA world like this - traffic levels are extremely high, the number of NPCs on the streets is ridiculous, it always feels like something's happening around every corner (there are so many random encounters!), you'll find loads of buildings you can go into, there's so much detail on everything... it's just an absolute dream for anyone who loves the idea of immersing themselves in this game.

GTA 5 had an amazing open world too, but after going back and playing it for the purpose of this review, there are two major differences that stand out - there's far less actually happening in the world at any one time (and therefore much less to interact with), and the map just feels tiny in comparison. GTA 6's state of Leonida incorporates so much more than just Vice City itself, including many other highly-populated areas such as Key Lento and Ambrosia. The first time you actually see Vice City in a mission (assuming you haven't gone and explored it previously) is a highlight of the entire game - it immediately appears so vast and so incredibly detailed that it feels like a next-gen experience.

The way in which you interact with that world as a player has evolved as well. Cops are smarter than ever, and not only prove a tough challenge when attempting a getaway at three stars or more, but they also remember what you look like - and therefore you sometimes have to disguise yourself by changing into different outfits. Stealing a car now requires you to think about what kind of lock system it has on it, and whether there's a tracker fitted that will alert the police to your location. Cars can even run out of fuel now! Every element feels more in-depth than we've seen in GTA in the past, but Rockstar has crucially balanced the impact just right, so it's never to the detriment of your ability to just have fun.

I do think you'll get the most out of the game if you pace yourself though. It feels intentionally designed to encourage a slow playstyle where you explore, hang out, browse the fully-featured social media and news feeds on your phone (complete with video clips and comment sections), take part in games like pool and minigolf, engage in countless side-missions and random encounters, watch and play a ridiculous amount of purpose-built content on your in-game TV, and ultimately just see what you can discover without rapidly jumping from mission-to-mission. The amount of content here is overwhelming, but in a really satisfying way.

Of course, it's almost a given at this point that GTA 6 looks visually incredible, and I can confirm that it's definitely a stunner on Xbox Series X. There's some occasional pop-in, but it's minimal, and I only ran into a few tiny bugs during the review period (which may have been ironed out for release anyway). The performance is mostly very smooth considering the circumstances as well - yes, it's a bit jarring at first to go back to 30FPS if you've been playing 60FPS games for the most part in recent years, but give it an hour-or-two, and you probably won't care anymore. Seriously, it's a total non-issue for me at this point, and I'm more than happy playing at 30FPS.

It should be noted that I played around 30 hours on a VRR-enabled display during the review period, and around 10 hours without one. I was perfectly happy with the performance in both cases, with the only noticeably big frame rate drops occurring during very rare and visually intensive gameplay sequences.

So, is there anything I don't like about GTA 6? The only thing I'd say is that it doesn't top my tier list in terms of greatest GTA stories ever, although it's probably still in the top three. It's a narrative that'll fully invest most players from start to finish, and there are shocking moments and twists that are bound to last long in the memory, but I also reckon it gets a bit too convoluted and farcical at times. That said, the final third of the campaign is jam-packed with intense story elements and incredibly action-packed missions, guaranteeing some truly jaw-dropping moments.

Its tone can also feel overly harsh and uncomfortably serious in specific circumstances, but hey... this is Grand Theft Auto after all. Every GTA has its moments like that, but the impact feels more striking this time due to the enhanced sense of realism. Fortunately, there's plenty of lighthearted humour to be found along the way as well.

Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated.

I'd have been fuming if you'd told me in 2013 that I'd have to wait 13 more years for the next GTA game, but now that it's finally here, I'm just relieved they've somehow managed to pull off another Game of the Decade contender once again.

#4002. Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off A Third Of Its Staff

Firaxis, the studio behind the Civilization series, has laid off around 60 employees, representing a third of its staff. The report comes from Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier.

In a statement provided to Bloomberg by a spokesperson from 2K, a subsidiary of Firaxis' owner, Take-Two, “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”

In addition to the 60 affected staffers, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is also departing. Bloomberg also reports, via anonymous Firaxis employees speaking to the outlet, that the studio is working on an unannounced XCOM game that has had a challenging development, with the team recently missing an important development milestone. This project, if it releases, will be the first Firaxis-developed XCOM game since XCOM: Chimera Squad in 2020.

Firaxis’ most recent release is Civilization VII, which launched in February 2025 to favorable reviews but initially "slow" sales, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick last August.  The game currently has a Mixed reception on Steam after Firaxis spent the last year updating the game to address player complaints. Before Civilization VII, Firaxis shipped Marvel's Midnight Suns in 2022, another critically well-received game that failed to meet sales expectations.

#4001. PlayStation Has No GOTY Nominee at The Game Awards for First Time in 12 Years

For the first time in 12 years — since all the way back in 2014 — there is no Sony-published PlayStation title amongst The Game Awards' Game of the Year nominees.

In that time, Sony has won three Game of the Year awards at Geoff's annual show, making it the most successful publisher in the event's history.

But its over-a-decade streak of nominations will finally come to an end here in 2026, as none of its releases from this year have made the cut.

That includes God of War: Sons of Sparta, Marathon, MLB The Show 26, Saros, Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, and Marvel's Wolverine.

In particular, Saros and Marvel Tokon got really strong reviews, but given just how stacked this year's competition is, it's no real surprise to see these relatively niche titles be left in the cold.

At the start of the year, many would have probably predicted that Wolverine would be in the mix — but a lukewarm critical reception has ultimately sealed its fate.

Just to recap, this year's Game of the Year nominees are as follows:

Again, since 2015, there hasn't been a single year where a Sony-published title has been ignored. Here's a full list of Sony's nominees in that time:

I don't think anyone would deny that Sony and its PlayStation Studios have had an off year. While their output has actually been quite frequent, none of their latest releases have made a lasting impact in the way that many of the above titles did in their respective years.

Do you think any of Sony's 2026 PS5 games deserved to be nominated for Game of the Year? Claw something out in the comments section below.

#4000. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

#3999. Grand Theft Auto VI Review - Outrageous Fortune

Many superlatives will be heard in the discussion around Grand Theft Auto VI – biggest world, most activities, best graphics, deepest narrative – but its real triumph is the way all those features and others work in service of a cohesive, believable immersion in a criminal fantasy that is hard to grasp until you’ve played it for yourself.

Rockstar’s latest returns players to a dramatically expanded version of the Vice City seen in a prior game, now largely unrecognizable after real and in-game years have passed. Leonida is a joy to explore, filled with a wealth of activities, both mundane and illicit. The game’s design makes many ordinary tasks as compelling as the illegal ones. Go fishing off the boat, brew coffee to wake up, work out at the gym, scuba dive for long-lost treasure, dust crops, motocross in the mud, go dancing at the club. As you move between those activities, the world feels alive with minor events, from traffic accidents to shady individuals a little too interested in your walk to the ATM. GTAVI delights in life's minutiae, with animations, voice lines, and background characters that keep things fresh even dozens of hours into the story. The level of detail everywhere is astounding and, at times, overwhelming. Getting sidetracked is easy.

The focus on detail carries into the visuals. Lucia’s hair blows in the wind, and she absently pushes it back behind her ear. A drug den is littered with paraphernalia and empty containers. A shifty contact quirks a smile – your only hint that things are about to go south. Sweat glistens on your character’s skin after a hard workout, their breathing and heart rate noticeably heightened. Clouds roll together in the sky, creating realistic weather simulations. The commitment to an authentic simulated world is encompassing, thoughtful, and intentional, a testament to hand-crafted and meticulously painstaking development work, paying off in an absorbing play-space that is hard to step away from.

While the day-to-day simulation is fascinating, it also adds pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward. Not even one of these meticulously choreographed sequences deserves to be spoiled; they run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect.

Ranged combat is punchy and enjoyable; smart use of cover and time-slowing focus makes most battles manageable. On-foot navigation is in a similar boat – simple to pick up and uninterested in needless complexity or challenge; the focus is on choosing smart moments for stealth, knowing when to run and when to fight, and selecting the precise instant for a burst of sudden action. Driving is fast and intense, made more appealing by a huge variety of functionally distinct vehicles to enjoy. If there’s a fault to the core and optional story missions, it’s that many feel a bit on rails regarding where to go and what to do at each step. At the same time, that directed approach keeps the pace relentless, and the action and outcomes thrilling. Over many hours, the game morphs and throws new wrenches into the mix at key junctures, teasing and then playing out criminal experiences from petty theft to group heists to illicit spec ops, and punctuates those distinct vibes with memorable and singular moments.

Like its predecessors, GTAVI simultaneously lampoons and celebrates life in modern America, taking aim at targets like social media, wellness lifestyles, rap and music culture, manosphere content, and dozens more. The caricatures land so well because, in many cases, they’re (sadly) barely over the line of the absurdity we see reflected in real life, and because Rockstar so ably captures individual subcultures, dialects, and situations. Behind it all is a scathing critique of wealth inequality and the inherent unfairness of a system that sets most up to fail. It’s a bitter message delivered in honey-wrapped, exhilarating gameplay, but it shines through.

Of all its significant feats, the relationship between Lucia and Jason elevates the game to new heights, lending this installment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries. This is, without a doubt, video gaming’s most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you’re left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts. The two collectively suffer the slings and arrows of a world that always seems stacked against them; the fortune they amass is not a power grab, but a desperate attempt to cling to each other and come out the other side together, and the player can’t help but cheer them on and dread how fate might stand in the way.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a generational game that stands toe-to-toe with many of the great crime stories and satires across other media. It showcases both the entertainment value of interactive play and the current high-water mark for technical and artistic detail in games. Hunt for and count up all the minor faults or foibles you like, but then note how you just spent another hour lost in this remarkable escape into criminality, wanton violence, egregious sex, and the elusive potential of true love.

Alex Van Aken contributed to this article.

#3998. Diablo 4's next season won't have any new mechanics or a new theme because all the focus is on Lord of Hatred

If you don't intend to buy the Lord of Hatred expansion, the next season in Diablo 4 won't be as exciting as you'd expect.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

A new update has landed for Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight on Switch 2.

#3996. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

#3994. Layoffs Hit XCOM Dev as It Struggles with Production of Third Entry

A third of Firaxis staff to lose their job

XCOM and Midnight Suns studio Firaxis Games has lost roughly one-third of its workforce in a round of layoffs today.

Around 60 people lost their jobs, and studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving the developer.

In a statement, a spokesperson said the team is "restructuring and recentering" around "designing world class strategy games". As a result, Firaxis is being downsized to focus on "design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis."

Quite how cutting one-third of your overall staff only now means you can refocus on making the best strategy games in the business makes little sense to me.

Apparently, the developer does actually have a third XCOM game in the works, but it's been hit with development issues. The Bloomberg report from Jason Schreier said Firaxis Games missed a "significant milestone over the summer".

Development of the game continues, but it may be affected by today's layoffs.
