#3943. Anticipated Warhammer 40K tactical RPG Dark Heresy gets a release date

Owlcat Games has revealed a release date for its tactical role-playing sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy. The game arrives 28th January, 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X. A Switch 2 release date will be provided "at a later date", a press release says.

Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy follows the good work laid down by Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader a couple of years ago. "Rogue Trader nails the 40k setting and provides an appropriately massive narrative filled with meaty tactical combat, though some bugs and poor performance hold it back," wrote Caeyln Ellis in Eurogamer's Warhammer 40,000 Rogue Trade review.

Dark Heresy changes things by casting you as an Inquisitor and tasking you with hunting down heretics and purging the world of dark influences, as one is wont to do in the 41st century, it seems. And developer Owlcat has apparently overhauled many of the systems underpinning the adventure.

There's a beta that's been running for a while that offers a complete first Act to try, and it's accessible if you buy a Founders edition of the game. This beta, incidentally, disappears 7th January, when Owlcat prepares the game for launch.

Meanwhile, Owlcat is making a substantially different RPG based around the popular Expanse license - a game that's much more closely inspired by Mass Effect. That project recently recruited the help of former Dragon Age writer David Gaider, and it will no doubt hope to fill a much-lamented hole created recently by the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.

#3942. Cyberattack on Sega third-party newsletter distributor reportedly sees over two million email addresses leaked, but Sega accounts unaffected

Japanese email distribution firm Arara were the target of the attack

Sega have revealed that over two million email addresses have leaked due to a cyberattack on Japanese email delivery provider Arara, whom the Like A Dragon and Sonic publishers use to distribute newsletters. Sega and Arara are currently busy investigating what happened in the breach, which doesn't appear to have affected the Sega accounts you can use receive in-game rewards and access a calendar which reminds you when it's Kazuma Kiryu's birthday. The companies have urged those who signed up for the affected newsletters to be wary of potential phishing attempts.

According to Automaton, who've translated Sega's official press release about the cyberattack, 2,196,044 email addresses in total were affected. 92,273 of that number were linked to the newsletter distribution.

The company have listed some specific newsletter releases as having been affected, including two exhibition announcements for this year's Tokyo Game Show, the announcement of arcade rhythm game Chunithm Mate's launch, six newsletters about online character lottery service Sega Lucky Kuji Online, the launch of a rhythm game update dubbed Ongeki Re:Fresh Act.2, and the launch of another arcade rhythm game update called Maimai DX MAGiCAL. Number one, that's a lot of rhythm games, and number two, Sega have advised those who opted in and received those newsletters to watch out for fishing emails from people posing as being tied to Sega or Arara.

Sega reportedly confirmed that - as far as the affected emails go - no names, dates of birth, genders, residential addresses, phone numbers, credit card information, and passwords are known to have been leaked. There had also been no reports of cases where the leaked information had been misused as of the time Sega made their announcement. The company have naturally put distributing any further email newsletters through Arara on hold until their investigation's done and plan to reach out to each affected person individually once the full details of the leak have been confirmed.

While data breaches and cyberattacks are nothing new, there have been a fair few recently, with both Street Fighter makers Capcom and Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 devs Warhorse suffering incidents of their own last month.

You can build (or neglect) the romance and relationship between Jason and Lucia in GTA 6

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Romance in GTA 6 isn't something you should shy away from. Rockstar Games' latest open-world crime epic follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as the pair reunite in Leonida. Whether they stick to being partners in crime or develop a healthy relationship status in GTA 6 is completely up-to you, with the connection between the two playable characters strengthening or weakening depending on your approach to the world. Jason and Lucia's relationship status isn't determined by completing certain missions or ticking off a few optional objectives, but rather it can change based on your actions, choices, and the time you spend together. Small acts of everyday affection and kindness will grow a healthier relationship in GTA 6, while ignoring your partner will slowly drive them apart.

There are four relationship statuses in GTA 6. You can move between each status at any time, organically depending on how you choose to play. You can track Jason and Lucia's relationship status at any time by holding right on the d-pad or by heading into the Jason & Lucia menu. They are (from least to most):

Tip: Jason and Lucia will remain connected as criminal partners throughout all of the GTA 6 missions, regardless of how their romantic relationship develops. However, certain moments in the story and interactions with characters may change depending on their relationship status at the time.

The process of building up your GTA 6 relationship status is organic – it happens gradually, over time through daily acts of affection and small acts of kindness. It's the smallest things that can make a difference, like greeting your partner when you meet up, buying them a snack, restocking their ammunition at an Ammu-Nation, or by holding hands while you explore the city together.

The bond between Jason and Lucia can also improve if you take time to do different activities together. Completing robberies and hitting gang hideouts together will strengthen their relationship, as will doing workouts together at the gym, and enjoying sports and leisure activities as a couple.

A little heart icon will appear on the screen beneath your health bar if you do something that your partner appreciates. Here's just a few examples of ways to improve your relationship status in GTA 6:

Tip: There are loads of ways to interact with your partner and collaborate in the world, more of which we detail in our guide to switching characters in GTA 6.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

To have the strongest relationship in GTA 6, both Jason and Lucia need to contribute to it. You can switch characters by holding right on the d-pad and then pressing R1. If you prioritize playing as one character over the other while you're playing, don't be surprised if the relationship naturally begins to degrade – this will impact the story and interactions between the two in a myriad of ways.

If you'd like to take more deliberate actions to lower your relationship status in GTA 6, then you certainly can do so. If you start ignoring your partner's calls and messages, don't be surprised if they start getting a little short with you on WhatUp. Spending lots of time apart, abandoning your partner while traveling together, or otherwise failing to engage with them on a daily basis will drive the two apart.

Tip: Small acts of affection will always help to improve the bond between Jason and Lucia, but if one of them has a GTA 6 Criminal Profile of 'Irredeemable' the relationship may never recover.

No, you cannot romance other characters beyond Lucia and Jason, at least through my experiences. I played through GTA 6 for over 100 hours and have yet to encounter any real opportunity to form a relationship or romance with any characters beyond those two, suggesting that their relationship is not an open one.

#3940. Hollow Knight Silksong physical editions mention multiple "free content packs" incoming, and call Sea of Sorrow a "giant expansion"

More than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong are finally arriving on players' doorsteps. It's the same brilliant and sometimes thrillingly cruel Metroidvania Eurogamer gave five stars to, except this time a pack-in booklet seemingly reveals the existence of multiple "free content packs" alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC.

Hollow Knight: Silksong's physical editions were originally set to be delivered from 10th November, but some early handovers have given us a peek inside the box. Redditor Me_975 posted pictures of their Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, and there's a few interesting tidbits tucked away - most notably in the manual's chapter on Content Packs.

"The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet reads. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with new friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!"

Developer Team Cherry confirmed plans for post-launch Silksong support last year, but remained pretty tight-lipped about what exactly that would look like. The indie outfit then announced the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow expansion, though we now have proper confirmation there's more content packs still to come, which shouldn't be a huge shocker considering all the free post-launch love Hollow Knight (the first one) received.

Speaking of Sea of Sorrow, that's mentioned here too: "In the first giant expansion, voyage across and beneath a salt-stricken ocean brimming with mystery and menace."

Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - time's a-ticking, Team Cherry. Still no release date so far, but the booklet does say it's "Coming Soon." Of course, Team Cherry are quite infamous for working on games until they balloon wildly out of control. After all, Silksong was once upon a time intended to be a Hollow Knight DLC, but with games this detailed, I can't really complain about waiting a little extra.

If you are interested in owning Silksong physically, it comes with a big map of Pharloom and the rest of the booklet also includes some really lovely art seemingly ripped straight from the game, as well.

#3939. Swarmbreaker is an uncommonly mesmerising tower defence game in which enemies "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid"

It is said that King Canute once placed his throne on the shore and commanded the sea not to get his feet wet, thus proving to his flattering courtiers that only God Almighty holds sway over the elements. "But sire!" I would have told him, if I'd been one of the aforesaid lickspittles. "Why not lay down spike strips and park a couple of flamethrowers in the shallows?" I would have said this because I have just been playing Swarmbreaker, a tower defence game that aims to prove there is no fluid body so awe-inspiring that it cannot be machine-gunned into submission.

In Swarmbreaker - which launches on Steam tomorrow, and still has a demo as of writing – you have to defend your rocketship against waves of insect aggressors, who spawn at the map's far corners. Between waves, you spend earnings from kills on turrets, barricades, troops, and upgrades for all the foregoing. Sounds like bog-standard attrition management, perhaps, but what lifts Swarmbreaker is the "swarm" part. The rapacious scuttlers come in several distinct varieties, but they also "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid".

The results are hypnotic: coloured particles burst from each burrow and course through the map's contours, pushing movable terrain elements and eroding your structures like acid. You can practically hear the oil derricks fizz as they are engulfed and chewed to a lumpy puddle of iridescent digestive enzymes. Speaking of which, the more oil derricks you save during each wave, the more cash you'll have to spend before the next, but committing to their protection obviously risks leaving your ship exposed. Your fallback option is an inexhaustible mouse-click-fired artillery cannon, but this won't save you if the bulk of the swarm makes it all the way to your doorstep.

I'm still not convinced this isn't a run-of-the-mill tower defender, beneath it all, but it's worth giving the demo a shot just to enjoy the swirling tidal dynamics of homocidal buglife. What would King Canute have made of it all? I think he would have stuck his throne right by the biggest burrow, surrounded by gravity traps and howitzers. "Back in your hole, hungry liquids!" he'd have bellowed, firing dual AK47s simultaneously. "The only god I recognise is efficient chokepoint management! Death to sense-of-flow! Death to trickle-down politics!"

"SIRE," I'd have told him sternly. "You are getting your metaphors confused. And also that is a total waste of howitzers - those things are best placed on hills." Read more on Steam.

GTA 6 is currently going live across the world, and in doing so, its PS5 Trophy list has now been made public. Exophase has the full list, which comprises 55 Trophies, including a Platinum Trophy.

The big thing here is that — just like every other Rockstar title released from PS3 onwards — you'll need to achieve 100% completion to unlock every Trophy.

I've looked through the complete list, and there's nothing there I'd consider a spoiler; the Trophy names and descriptions are vague, so don't worry about having the ending spoiled or anything like that.

As stated, a Gold Trophy called A Long Road wants you to "attain 100% completion". Given how much content is packed into GTA 6, this could take you hundreds of hours to accomplish.

Alongside the requirements of the 100% completion, you've obviously got to complete the main story, win races and complete stunts, finish missions for specific characters (which I assume are side quests), and also succeed in an assortment of robberies.

Crystal Dynamics confirmed that eight people have been let go in a "necessary business decision."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Crystal Dynamics has confirmed that eight people have been let go in the latest round of layoffs at the beleaguered Tomb Raider studio.

"Crystal Dynamics made a difficult, but necessary business decision to reduce our current studio staff by eight people," the studio said of the layoffs, first reported by Vertical Slice, in a statement provided to PC Gamer.

"Whenever we phase roles off a project, we make every effort to find new spots for our great colleagues first. Everyone affected receives a full severance package as well as job placement assistance to aid them through this transition. We wish them the best and hope to work together in the future."

The studio added that no ongoing projects are impacted by the cuts.

In terms of raw numbers, eight people is not a huge cut, especially when compared to layoffs at other studios—Firaxis reportedly cut roughly 60 employees earlier today, for instance. But it's concerning in the case of Crystal Dynamics because the studio has been bleeding for so long: This is at least the fifth round of layoffs in less than two years, and comes just eight months after the last round of cuts. Roughly 70 employees in total have been let go over that span.

The studio has also struggled to get things done with its flagship series, Tomb Raider. Crystal Dynamics regained control of the property in 2022, shortly after the studio was acquired by Embracer, but in June Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, a remake of the original game, was delayed to February 2027; less than two months later, the all-new Tomb Raider: Catalyst was pushed into 2028. The studio also co-developed the Perfect Dark reboot alongside The Initiative for four years before Microsoft killed it in July 2025.

#3936. God of War: Ragnarok is reportedly the highest-earning PlayStation Studios game this generation, but Marvel's Spider-Man 2 isn't far behind

God of War: Ragnarok is the generation's best-selling and highest-earning PlayStation Studios game, according to a new report, but the full top 10 list has a few nice surprises.

In the four years since its PS5 release and two years since its PC port, God of War: Ragnarok has reportedly sold just over 20m copies and generated $1.4b in revenue, according to estimates from Alinea Analytics. About 27.5 percent of the 15m copies it sold on console came from physical editions, and the action blockbuster apparently sold a further 1.1m this year alone. Not bad, boy.

Those stats should bode well for the series' next romp God of War: Laufey - which sees Faye take the spotlight across a multi-mythological afterlife and was recently delayed into May 2027 - even if PlayStation moves away from PC ports for its signature single-player games.

Kratos and Atreus only narrowly beat out perhaps the biggest superhero of them all: Marvel's Spider-Man 2, a game that reportedly made a whopping $1.3b off 19.1m copies across PS5 and PC. The Spidey sequel should keep swinging even higher as the years chug on, though - the report states that sales always surge during the holiday months, and this year's big screen behemoth Spider-Man: Brand New Day led to an even bigger spike than usual.

Racing sim royalty Gran Turismo 7 ($841m), bug-squashing phenomenon Helldivers 2 ($786m), robo-dino sequel Horizon: Forbidden West ($485m), vengeful spirit sim Ghost of Yotei ($410m), undead remake The Last of Us Part 1 ($341m), multidimensional romp Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart ($334m), Stellar Blade ($316m) and delightful throwback Astro Bot ($292m) round out the top 10 games published by PlayStation Studios this generation.

It's worth noting that Helldivers 2 and Stellar Blade were developed by studios outside the PlayStation umbrella, but the console maker still published both upon release. Ghost of Yotei's performance is also particularly impressive since Sucker Punch's sequel has only been out for a year and didn't get the benefit of a PC port, like many of its PS5 siblings. The success couldn't save Sucker Punch from recent layoffs, however.

On PlayStation's decision to kill disc-based physical releases, analyst Rhys Elliott said that the bottom five games in the list together made $281.7m this year alone: "PlayStation wants those numbers to be bigger in the coming years, which is one of the reasons it's killing the disc (alongside the better margins it and publishers get through digital.)"

#3935. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy releases in January, leaving not very long to prepare for all the crunchy cRPG choices and secret wars it'll lob your way

Embrace the role of an Inquisitor in the grim darkness of the not so far away future

Oh shit, that's not too far away. Terrifyingly, that last sentence is now a thing I can accurately write about games coming out in January 2027. Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy has just been confirmed as one such game, with the cRPG's heresy investigation set to commence towards the end of the month.

January 28th, 2027, is the full Dark Heresy release date, as announced by devs Owlcat on Steam. The beta version of the game'll be closing down on January 7th to make way for the full game, so as of writing there's still some time to give that a go if you fancy.

If this is the first you've heard of Dark Heresy, here's Owlcat's synopsis of what it's all about:

Embrace the role of an Inquisitor in the grim darkness of the far future in a cRPG set in the rich Warhammer 40,000 universe. Start your service as an acolyte of the Inquisition: Investigate heresy, command a diverse warband, and shape the fate of the Calixis Sector in a story-rich experience where every decision has weight, justice is non-existent, and the line between salvation and damnation is razor-thin. Explore an in-depth depiction of the Inquisition as an organisation and the vast force it commands: its power, bureaucracy, and inner conflicts laid bare like never before.

As an Inquisitor, you have one primary goal: to protect the Imperium, whether that be from the taint of xenos, the betrayal of heretics, or the scourge of mutants, by any means necessary. Be the conduit of the Emperor’s will in a place where all hope was lost decades ago, explore the mysteries of the maddening Tyrant Star, and overcome the worst horrors thrown at you by the Noctis Aeterna.

A place where all hope was lost decades ago? You sure this is the Warhammerverse and not real life lads? I jest, but bursting into rooms and shouting 'Nobody expects the God-Emperor’s inquisition!' Monty Python-style does sound quite fun. Oisin's previously written in more depth about what Dark Heresy devs have said regarding what to expect from its investigations, if you want nitty-gritty details rather than references to sketch comedy.

If you're so inclined, Dark Heresy is wishlistable on Steam.

#3933. "Something's really possible" - Mass Effect cast rally around efforts to save the franchise on the first N7 Day after BioWare's closure

I'm Commander Shepard and this is my favorite video on the internet.

This N7 Day was the first without developer BioWare around, but fans of the Mass Effect series didn't let 7th November go by quietly. The community managed to get several notable Mass Effect actors to lend their voice to the increasingly loud 'SaveMassEffect' movement.

In the weeks since BioWare's shock closure and Mass Effect Universe's cancellation, the community-organised We Are Mass Effect group have put up billboards in Times Square, a mobile billboard outside BioWare Edmonton's former office and much more while directing attention to an online petition.

Today is a very special day for Mass Effect fans. We've worked incredibly hard to bring together most of the original Mass Effect trilogy's voice cast to share a very important message with you. We need to #SaveMassEffect. https://t.co/FOp0qp4wBI

And for the series' annual celebration, the group managed to get a sizable portion of the Mass Effect cast to join in. Commander Shepard actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, original trilogy composer Sam Hulick, Garrus' Brandon Keener, Jack's Courtnay Taylor, Tali'Zorah's Ash Sroka, Thane's Keythe Farley and many more all showed up in a two-minute video to help potentially salvage the series - sometimes in character.

"When we heard about the formal closing of Boware, I felt weirdly hopeful," Hale said in a separate interview with IGN. "I can't explain it. I just got so weirdly hopeful. My first thought, of course, was for the devs and all the people. And then I just closed my eyes and crossed my fingers and I said, 'I feel something's possible. You know, something's really possible.'"

The other half of Commander Shepard, Mark Meer, noted that "this didn't all just happen in the last 10 days." Near yearly layoffs at EA had slowly trimmed multiple BioWare teams down, sometimes even affecting studio veterans who had been at the company for decades.

"A lot of senior writers within the last year or two were let go. People who had been there from the very beginning. Again, people who had built that company from the ground up, who built the bones of it, who made those games that had captured people so much right back from the 1990s," Meer said.

#3932. Don't be fooled by Horses of Hoofprint Bay's hand-drawn art, this stable management game has all the drama of a Jilly Cooper novel

Poema is my pride and joy. She was my first horse and she's a competition winner, but she's reached her potential. She'll never be a show jumper, and that's where the money and prestige are to be found. If I'm ever to grow my horse farm into a nationally renowned equestrian centre, I need the cash to expand and upgrade my facilities. Poema is a hoofstep on the path to that future, but she's not going to be able to take me all the way herself.

For all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface. While the game's scripted narrative may be lacking, it's shockingly easy to fill in the gaps with drama worthy of a Jilly Cooper novel.

There may be better author comparisons, but I learned everything I know about showjumping from Cooper's Riders – much as I learned everything about independent television franchise bids in the '80s from its sequel Rivals – a book which is as much about the nitty gritty of horsetraining and competing as it is about toffs jumping into bed with one another. In my mind the two are tightly connected - showjumping and Jilly Cooper, not horses and toff bonking. In Horses of Hoofprint Bay, the only real story you get is the fact you've scrimped and saved to buy your first horse and your uncle has lent you the use of his field while you start your business. I was hoping there would at least be a similar setup to Regency Solitaire, where your motivation for touring the country's tearooms is motivated by paying off your brother's gambling debts. Yet, despite this disappointing start, I soon found its business simulation mechanics provide great storytelling material.

Horses of Hoofprint Bay has many of the trappings of a cosy game. At the start of each day, you'll prepare the stables, dragging a rake around the yard to sling away the manure, clicking buckets of water to refill the trough, and making sure there's enough hay for all the horses. But this isn't just for the larks, if you skip these tasks there are serious knock on effects for yours horses. Forget to brush down your horses' coats or pick out the stones in their shoes, and they're liable to develop saddle sores and other injuries when you ride them. Leave an abrasion untreated and it can develop into an infection. Even something like taking a dirty horse to a contest can cost you. I forgot to brush Poema before entering her into her first contest and despite taking first place, her embarrassingly unkempt coat lost my stable prestige. It was a cruel end to what should have been a great celebration.

So long as your horses are well rested, you can train them each day. You may want to take them through some confidence building lunges, where they need to walk, trot, and canter on demand, or a more physically demanding Cavaletti or showjumping course. These latter too are much more tiring, but they build a horse's strength and endurance. The higher its endurance the more energy it can expend on training sessions each day, and the higher its strength the more jumps it can do in succession before slowing to a walk for a breather - essential when you're competing in a timed competition. Overdo the exercise, however, and you'll exhaust a horse, severely reducing its energy for the next day.

Now, unlike Poema, my freshly bought stallion Kolizey has the potential to compete in showjumping competitions. He'll never go all the way to the big national contests, but he can take a ribbon in the district and regional contests. Or he will when he's up to standard; he's arrived from the breeder in a sorry state: brambles in his mane, mud on his flanks, stones in his shoes, and his strength and endurance are far too low to make it through an entire course of obstacles.

The biggest problem, however, is Kolizey's confidence: it's shot. I don't know what was happening in the stalls at the breeder's, but he arrived at my stables backing up at the first sign of a jump. Before I can hope to earn him his first ribbon, I have to build up our relationship. If we exercise together enough in the yard, his confidence will grow and he will follow my direction without question.

It may be getting ahead of myself, but I also have plans for Kolizey and Poema to produce a foal. Done right, the two should raise a horse that's able to exceed its parents' potential, becoming stronger and more endurant than both of them. A stronger horse means a ticket to the bigger contests and the bigger prize pots. Not that I can start breeding the two just yet. I want both horses to be at peak physical fitness. Poema's already there, while Kolizey can't even manage a jump without shying away.

While getting Koliszey contest ready, I still need to be bringing in cash. That means using Poema as a training horse for students' riding lessons. The better I am at the minigame where I use the Q, E, W, A, S, and D keys to tell them to sit forward or back, hold the reins higher or lower, or to level out their legs, the more they tip me. I have to be careful, because when Poema is working with students, she's not being stretched, and her strength and endurance can wither which means she struggles to maintain her winning streak in the contests.

Another reason to hold off on getting Poema pregnant is that during the second half of her pregnancy, she can't be ridden, which means no contests and no lessons for students. Currently, those are my two main sources of income besides what I'm paid in rent to board a couple of nearby farmers' horses. I don't want her out of the rota when Kolizey isn't yet ready to step into her place.

And, well, while I'm on the subject of plans, reader, I must tell you, the future lies in semen. If I can build the facilities, earn the cash, and raise Kolizey's profile, I can make a good buck on his virile stallion cream. With the money I bring in from a prizewinning semen I can expand into the far field, creating space to take on more horses, upgrade my home from the caravan I'm living in currently, maybe even build a proper training school. I'm not going to afford all that by giving riding lessons to the local children or boarders' rent. No, the big money comes from competition wins and valuable horse sauce.

While Poema continues entering contests and carrying students, I start pushing Kolizey harder. Multiple training sessions every day. I begin with Cavaletti, which is a kind of obedience competition. Your horse has to be travelling at the correct speed when it passes marker flags – walking, trotting, or cantering – and make some small jumps over cross bars. It should be straightforward, but because Kolizey's confidence is so low, he keeps refusing my orders and trying to change speed. He warns me before he's about to speed up or slow down, and if I counter it in time he will obey me and even receive a little confidence boost, but often he does it just before a jump, messing up my timing and he hits the bars. Each time he fails a jump it knocks his confidence, risking me taking me even further from where I need him to be.

I try the easier lunges sessions. And they raise his confidence a little but they're doing little for his physical health. It's all taking too long and Poema's getting older every day. In a fit of frustration, and in mark that I may not be able to cut it as an animal trainer, I skip from the Cavaletti training straight into a showjumping qualifier. The time limits on these are much stricter, so you have to clear the course at a gallop. This is also where a horse's strength really comes into play. The faster you're going, the more strength it requires to jump an obstacle. Horses only recover strength when moving at a walk, so you don't want to tire a horse out by going at a gallop through the whole course, else they won't have the strength to make all the jumps and they'll be forced to withdraw from the event. But nor do you want to go too slowly and fall foul of the time limit.

I realise my mistake as soon as the course begins: I try to stir Kolizey into a walk he refuses. Thankfully the timer only starts when he crosses the line, but it's an inauspicious start. I tap forward again and he begins to walk. I tap again and Kolizey moves up to a trot, then to a canter, before picking up to a gallop. I think he's going too fast as we approach the first jump, but Kolizey clears it. Then another jump and another. With a nervous eye on the depleting strength bar, I tap him down to a canter for the next jump. We're halfway through the course, I briefly slow to a walk to recover some strength then take the next three jumps at a canter. We're so close to the end now but a big yellow exclamation mark appears next to the strength bar. Kolizey is on the edge of exhaustion but he refuses to slow down and increases to a gallop for the last two jumps.

He completes the course with a perfect clear. Not a single obstacle clipped and we end with ten seconds left on the timer. Not only has Kolizey earned his showjumping license, his success swells his confidence. He's a natural athlete.

The next day, with my horses rested, I take Kolizey and Poema to town to compete in the showjumping and Caprilli events respectively. They both bring home first place, raising the prestige of my stables, earning me a tidy little packet, and convincing me it's time my prized horses started a family. I'm perhaps too eager, when I try to send them to the breeding station, I'm told they're both 'Done for the day'. I suppose I should give my contest winners a bit of a break. They've earned it. I groom them and send them both to bed with an apple as a treat.

Except, maybe they weren't too tired: the next morning, I'm met with a message telling me Poema is pregnant. My stable's become the Olympic Village, with my rosette-winning horses working out the highs and stresses of competition in the only way they know how. Good on them. I needn't have even made the breeding station.

Then, with horror, I remember the horses I'm boarding for the neighbours. They're both stallions themselves. Neither of them are at competition level, their strength and endurance is lower even than Poema's when she arrived at the stable. If either of them are the father, Poema is about to be out of action for a whole season and at the other end of it I'll have a foal that can't even compete in the beginner events. fetch the equestrian version of Hercule Poirot, I need to find out who impregnated my horse!

It may not be a plot worthy of Cooper, but it will do for me.

#3931. Guide: GTA 6: Who Is the Real Actress Lucia Is Based On?

As one of the two main protagonists in GTA 6, you're going to spend a lot of time playing as Lucia. As such, you may be interested in learning more about the real-life actress she's based on. In this GTA 6 guide, we are answering: who is the real actress Lucia is based on in GTA 6?

GTA 6's Lucia is based on Manni L. Perez — the game uses both her voice and her likeness.

For months, she was rumoured and speculated to play Lucia in the game, but her involvement in GTA 6 was confirmed by her nomination in the Best Performance category at The Game Awards. She now also appears in the GTA 6 credits.

At the time of the game's release, Perez is 34 and resides in the USA.

She's been an actress since 2013, and GTA 5 was actually where she made her debut. Perez lent her voice to a clubber in GTA 5, and then she did the same for a blackjack dealer in GTA Online. Now, she's sharing the leading role with Jason in GTA 6.

Perez lent her voice to the GTA Online blackjack dealer, as seen in this video:

Perez has also appeared in a number of different TV shows, from 2017 to 2025, including:

Huang announced that he would accept reinstatement, but Nvidia isn't offering it.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week after details about multiple extramarital affairs came to light, will not be allowed to un-resign, says the company.

"On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," said Nvidia chairman Harvey C. Jones during a regularly scheduled investors call today. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

Huang was open to the idea of returning: After AI enthusiasts and tech CEOs including Tim Sweeney and Elon Musk rallied around the former CEO, he said that he would return to Nvidia if the board came calling.

"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," Huang said in a statement to press. "If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO."

At the same time, reports circulated that the Nvidia board was not interested in having him back, which Jones has now stated in no unclear terms.

The Nvidia chairman went on to recap the actions Nvidia has taken since Huang's resignation, which include putting CFO Colette Kress in charge as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement and establishing a "national security and export control oversight committee."

The affair Huang admitted to, before reports of others came out, was with a suspected Chinese spy. China has denied the accusation of espionage.

#3929. GTA 6 pre-orders are tracking "well above expectations" and the game will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two, says CEO Strauss Zelnick

Today, as part of Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick noted that pre-orders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are tracking "far above expectations", and is certain that soon "numbers will speak for themselves" when it comes to the game.

Zelnick also promised GTA Online and GTA 5 will continue to receive updates in order to support the "nearly 235 million" units sold to date across "an unprecedented three console generations". The GTA series as a whole has, to date, sold over 480 million units. Karl Statoff, president at Take-Two, adds the launch of GTA 6 will be a "defining moment for the company and global entertainment industry". Zelnick adds, later in a question and answer session, that he expects GTA 6 to "set a new baseline" for Take-Two. "The future's really bright across the board," he notes.

For the next quarter, Take-Two expects to deliver $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion - with "recurrent consumer spending" to raise by 12 percent, driven by "the groundbreaking release" of Grand Theft Auto 6, and expects to see "significant growth for the Grand Theft Auto series", driven by sales of - specifically - Grand Theft Auto 6's Ultimate Edition, which includes add-on content, and that most people are pre-ordering at its $100 price point. That bonus $20 between the $80 base edition and the Ultimate Edition is counted as "recurrent consumer spending", as is part of that massive bump the company has seen.

It also seems that we will see more GTA games - or content, at least - sooner than expected. "We do think that the nature and velocity of the content we'll see from our iconic franchises, including GTA, will look dramatically different over the next decade." It's a vague comment, but assumedly the work done on the engine and backend of GTA 6 means we'll see more content arriving in shorter order than we're used to for the series. This is per an article published by IGN in line with the earning's call going live.

Elsewhere in the earnings call, Take-Two referred to its current setup with its mobile, sports, 'core new IP' and 'core existing IP' as "the strongest development pipeline in the company's history". In terms of new IP, Zelnick directed investors to consider the launches of incoming projects like Ken Levine's mysterious Judas and Project Ethos (which we don't know too much about yet, other than it's billed as a "roguelike hero shooter"). For core IP, 8 sequels and 7 remakes, remasters, and platform extensions.

Buoyed by these plans, Zelnick outlines that he believes that fiscal year 2027 "will be a historic year for Take-Two" as the company is buoyed by "recent and upcoming releases". No prizes for what that's referring to. If you're curious about what sort of numbers we may be looking at here, all you need to do is cast your mind back to 2014, where you will remember GTA 5 made $1bn in just three days.

#3928. Big Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

Friendslop du jour Big Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game."

A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset. House House explain that they couldn't find a solution themselves, asked a Unity engineer for help who said it was impossible, and then decided the only answer was to ask an LLM chatbot; "after a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code." While absolutely not the most pressing thing to mention here, it is very funny to me for House House to clarify that they "had to modify the suggestion extensively", almost as if this tech isn't actually helpful in giving useful answers.

So, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove. The thing is, this wasn't a case of being forced to by upper management, as is sometimes the case. This was a choice made entirely voluntarily, and House House are attempting to have their cake and eat it by ending their statement with the reflection that "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards." But then, you know, that's followed up by saying that Big Walk was developed "without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." So, not to worry, they learned touching the stove is bad by touching the stove, and definitely won't do it again in future. If only there were thousands of other cases informing them why touching the stove is bad.

Very relevant to this reveal is the recent statement by select jurors of the Independent Games Festival which, after much internal deliberation, came to the conclusion that those who sign the statement would decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, with signees including Austin Walker, Sam Barlow, Lena Reine, Brendon Chung, Aura Triolo, aurahack and more. The statement specifies that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms." Fellow juror Liz Ryerson confirmed that Big Walk was being considered by the IGF, and was a matter of discussion in judging as to whether its use of genAI would be acceptable.

As for House House only disclosing this now, they state it was not only because it was necessary for their IGF submission, but also that "we have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage", and that they have spoken on it publicly to Aftermath because "it has become a matter of public interest."

If I were to be cynical, I would say that House House would prefer to be the ones breaking this news themselves rather than having the IGF reveal that they had been hiding their use up until now; it's usually easier to control PR if you release it yourself. Big Walk had already been securely in everyone's good books for its support for the BDS boycott, for example, so why ruin that clean rep with something like a genAI disclosure?

I don't know how better to close this article than with an excerpt from that very IGF statement:

"We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed "inevitable." As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

The future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together."

The additional content you unlock through pre-ordering GTA 6 or buying the Ultimate Edition is all found in different locations

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Are you wondering how to unlock the GTA 6 pre-order and GTA 6 Ultimate Edition bonuses? Don't worry, I was too through my first few hours in Leonida. It turns out that Rockstar Games doesn't want you having too many cool things too quickly, which is why you'll need to progress through different sections of the game before you'll gain access to unique weapons, vehicles, mod shops, clothing stores, and more that come as part of the DLC package, no matter which of the GTA 6 versions you own.

Below you'll find a breakdown of where to get the GTA 6 pre-order bonuses for both the Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition of the game. You'll also find a detailed breakdown of where to access all of the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition exclusives, which unlock as you progress through the story.

Regardless of whether you pre-ordered the Standard Edition or the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6, you'll get access to a couple of nice bonus items. These are available from Chapter 3 onwards, and can be unlocked by doing the following:

The option to collect a uniquely-styled '55 Vapid Stainer vehicle from Vice Beach will appear as a task within the Exploration section of the map index. Once you've collected the vehicle from outside the Ocean View Hotel, you'll also unlock the Bonita Court Garage north of Washington Beach to store it in.

Once you've collected your '55 Vapid Stainer vehicle, you'll unlock some other bonuses as well. Head back to your residence and access the wardrobe to find exclusive outfits, and then visit any Salon to access a new hairstyle for Jason and Lucia under the Special section of the in-store menu.

As soon as you've found the 55 Vapid Stainer, the first thing you'll want to do is drive across to any Ammu-Nation store. Once inside, access the weapons locker and head into the Cosmetics / Wraps section of the modify menu on any gun to freely apply the pre-order exclusive weapon pattern.

If you purchase the more expensive GTA 6 Ultimate Edition, you'll find that Rockstar has well and truly made it worth your while. The exclusive storefronts, weapons, clothes, and vehicles aren't immediately accessible, instead they become available once you reach certain GTA 6 mission milestones:

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Once you're able to leave Jason's House in Chapter 1, you'll find two exclusive vehicles waiting for you. Underneath the house you'll find an Army fatigue-tinged Dinka Enduro motorcycle in the driveway, and off to the back of the building you'll spot a Crest Kayak which can be used to explore the Leonida Keys.

Only available for use in Chapter 1, you can get an exclusive pro build for Jason's Vapid Ganado pickup truck. Open up the map and head into the Vehicles index, from there click the Mod Shops option and look for Coastal Auto Care in Key Lento. Drive the Vapid Ganado over there and the unlock can be applied inside the Pro Builds / Full Kits section of the mod shop menu.

Take Jason to any Ammu-Nation store from Chapter 1 and access the weapon locker to unlock a personalized Girardi ES9 pistol. You can do the same with Lucia from Chapter 2 onwards, unlocking a unique Klose K17 pistol. Both of these weapons are free to equip and use.

Once you're into Chapter 2 of GTA 6, you'll be able to access unique weapon variants of the powerful Morgan revolver (regardless of whether you've already purchased the weapon). Jason and Lucia have their own versions, which can be accessed from any Ammu-Nation weapon locker.

Located in North Leonard County, just north of Lake Leonida, you'll gain access to One-Eyed Willie's Auto Shop from Chapter 1. This GTA 6 Mod Shop specializes in off-road vehicles, and will give you access to a range of custom, hand-painted liveries for purchase.

Spend enough time meeting the locals at the Motel safehouse and you'll eventually meet Wyman, who will invite Lucia to the Thrillbilly Mud Club. Once you've completed a Dirt Track Race, look for a task in the exploration section of the map index to go collect your Dominator buggy and storage garage.

Once you have collected the Dominator buggy in Chapter 2, Wyman will contact you on WhatUp and ask for your help tracking down parts for classic cars. Look for the Find Cars for Wyman option in the exploration section of the map index to start this optional activity.

If you've got money to burn, then you'll want to take your favorite car over to Rideout Customs, located in the Crosstown district of Vice City. This Mod Shop offers unique interiors, rims, and stylings for any Donks vehicle classes. Head to the Vehicles map index and click the Mod Shops tab to set a destination.

Technically accessible from Chapter 1, there's a number of PTT YOUNGIN$ Compounds to raid for cash and key valuables. You'll need to head into Southside (south of Vice Dale County) to unlock these Illegal Operations. Once you've visited the area, head to the Robberies section of the map index.

Stock 305 can be found in the north quadrant of Vice City, in the Stockyard district. This skate store, selling contemporary streetwear and accessories, can be easily located by opening the map, heading to the style section of the index, and clicking onto the Casual & Street tab to get a destination.

Undoubtedly one of the better Hair & Beauty locations in GTA 6, Sara's Unisex Salon is located on the main strip of the Hamlet town. Find it in the Style section of map index. Once you're into Chapter 2, you'll gain access to exclusive signature looks for Jason and Lucia.

Located in the Stockyard area of Vice City, the Electric Fang Tattoo Parlor is open for business from Chapter 1. This tattoo parlor has over 50 signature tattoos for Jason and Lucia, all designed by the artist collective FAILE. Head to the Style section of the map index and look for the Tattoos tab.

The Wonder Whale is a Souvenir & Swimwear shop available for all players, located in the heart of the Key Leonto area (just off the main strip of highway). Head to the mannequins in the store to find some exclusive merch to purchase and wear. Just head to the Style section of the map index to get a location.

Once you're in Chapter 4, you've likely figured out the styles of both Jason and Lucia. Expect that to be challenged once a set of outfits are unlocked, for free – accessed directly from your wardrobe. A new set of tattoos are also available from most tattoo parlors, and new hair/beard styles at Sara's Unisex Salon.

Chapter 4 will also unlock a Shitzu Squalo for you to use for fishing and to search for dive sites in GTA 6. The boat is docked in a canal, south of the Washington Beach area of the map – just to the left of the Y Hotel. You can locate this vehicle at all times by heading to the Personal section of the map index.

An exclusive variant of one of the best cars in GTA 6 will be made available to you in Chapter 5. The '95 Grotti Cheetah is parked up in the garage beneath the Pegassi Residences building just waiting for you to collect it. You can also find a task in the Exploration section of the map index to help locate it.

#3926. As investors ask about GTA 6 and AI, Take-Two CEO once again puts faith in dev creativity, states making hit games "remains the purview of human beings"

"Making a big hit was hard then, and it's hard now, and it's going to be hard in the future."

Today, as part of Take-Two Interactive Software's Q2 2027 earnings call, Strauss Zelnick fielded questions from investors after presenting the financial results of the company. One caller was concerned about AI - specifically about the proliferation of AI-powered compilations and decompilations that have been raising piracy concerns for publishers over the past few weeks.

Zelnick notes that "[the video games] business has been largely immune to piracy" thanks to factors like file size, how console ecosystems work, and aspects related to the online nature of the games industry. That said, Strauss continues, there is a threat posed to the industry because of AI. However, he assures listening investors that Take-Two is appropriately scaling its measures against bad faith actors using artificial intelligence.

"We are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defences and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And - at the same time, without in any way being cavalier - every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy, [and] this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it."

Zelnick pivots back to AI again later in the call, where one investor once again asks about AI, seemingly keen to learn whether the CEO feels it can provide GTA 6 developer Rockstar with any kind of "competitive advantage" in the games industry. Given Zelnick's previous comments on the subject, his answer was not a complete surprise.

"It's always been true [that technology benefits us]," explains Zelnick. "We've always created our entertainment inside computers with technology. All advances have benefited us, and I don't expect that that will change - in fact, I hope it'll accelerate. I think at the same time, what we're known for [at Take-Two] is the desire to make the best entertainment on Earth. And, more often than not, we have succeeded - and the creativity that drives that success is human creativity harnessing technology. And I think that's what you'll see in the future, too.

"Undoubtedly some of the most recent technological advances that you've seen have made it easier to create assets. Where all that is consistent with the story of our business. When I started in interactive entertainment (longer ago than I would like to say), it was really difficult to create an asset in a computer. Today, it's a whole lot easier - but you know what's not easier? Making a big hit. Making a big hit was hard then, and it's hard now, and it's going to be hard in the future. And hit creation remains the purview of human beings."

This isn't the first instance of AI skepticism we've seen from Strauss Zelnick. Back in March, he outright rejected the idea that AI can tackle games on the scale of GTA 6. Elsewhere in the call, the Take-Two CEO reiterated how well GTA 6 is tracking as he reasserted pre-order numbers are well above expectations, and promised that the success of the game will "set a new baseline" for Take-Two's gaming business.

#3925. GTA 6 Base PS5 Performance Suffers 'Minor' and 'Sustained' Frame Rate Drops, But It's 'Unwavering' on PS5 Pro

As you'd expect, it sounds like PS5 Pro is the absolute best place to play GTA 6 at launch — but what about playing it on Sony's standard console? Our pals over at Digital Foundry have been putting it to the test.

First things first, Digital Foundry can't stress enough just how technically impressive Rockstar's latest open world is. In terms of simulating a living and breathing environment, it's completely unmatched — and that's the main reason why it's capped at just 30 frames-per-second with no graphics options to choose from.

On PS5 Pro, that 30fps is supposed to be "unwavering". The report describes performance as "exceptionally robust" with "perfect frame pacing" — meaning that the game feels super responsive despite its 30fps cap.

GTA 6 also benefits massively from the Pro's built-in PSSR upscaling tech, to the point where it "convincingly mimics native 4K" resolution. Compared to playing on the base PS5, the image clarity is noticeably sharper, especially when it comes to the smaller details (of which there are many).

But to be clear, it's not like GTA 6 is a mess on the base PS5 — it just comes with some drawbacks.

Alongside the aforementioned downgrade in visual clarity, the game struggles to maintain a solid 30fps at times. The frame rate holds up fine during general gameplay, but it looks like busier scenarios start to drag it down.

You can get "minor dips" when driving at speed, with more "sustained" drops occurring when you're partaking in especially hectic combat encounters, complete with explosions.

These bigger bouts of choppiness can reportedly see the frame rate drop down into the mid-20s, which is obviously far from unplayable, but it's certainly not ideal.

But again, Digital Foundry makes it clear that Rockstar had to compromise on overall performance to deliver on its ridiculously ambitious open world vision — which falls in line with what the developer told us here at Push Square.

News 'PS5 Pro Is Not Powerful Enough to Run GTA 6 at 60fps': Rockstar Explains Frame Rate Decision

Indeed, the analysis heaps praise on the game's borderline photorealistic lighting, and "arguably the best implementation of ray tracing we've seen to date". All in all, Digital Foundry's just blown away by the sheer level of detail that's on display at all times — which is also something that Sammy wrote about at length in his GTA 6 PS5 review.

But what do you make of this tech report? Are you playing GTA 6 on PS5 Pro, or PS5? Are you still disappointed by the 30fps cap? Feel free to wait for the inevitable PS6 version in the comments section below.

Review GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

Robert (or Rob if you're lazy) is an assistant editor of Push Square, and has been a fan of PlayStation since the 90s, when Tekken 2 introduced him to the incredible world of video games. He still takes his fighting games seriously, but RPGs are his true passion. The Witcher, Persona, Dragon Quest, Mass Effect, Final Fantasy, Trails, Tales — he's played 'em all. A little too much, some might say.

#3924. Following site-wide discussion on AI use, Nexus Mods add a "daily limit" to the spots in the new mods tab one person can hog via multiple rapid-fire uploads

It's a "stopgap solution" while the site's staff are busy "working on more sophisticated tools"

The folks behind Nexus Mods have rolled out a new "daily limit" system which ensures modders who upload multiple works in bulk during a single 24 hour period can't take up more than one spot in the tabs dedicated to showing off new mods for different games. Instead, those who chuck up their mods in bulk will see one of their works given a spot, while the rest are neatly filed away behind it, ready to spring out if you click a bit of text indicating that modder's got other fresh works to show off.

"Nexus Mods owner and CEO Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann hinted measures related to making the glut of new mods currently uploaded on a daily basis less of a discovery nightmare in last week's announcement post about the site's current policy regarding the use of genAI in mod making. "We’ve received feedback regarding authors uploading numerous mods at once and overwhelming the Recently Added section, pushing everyone else down the page," he wrote. "This is less of an issue related to AI, but it’s becoming much more prevalent as mod production is speeding up. Thus, we’re trying out limits on the number of mods from one author that can be shown in this section to give others a better chance of getting noticed. We’re also putting tighter restrictions on uploads from newly created accounts. The first of these updates will be available soon."

Cue an an announcement on Nexus Mods' Discord server yesterday by community manager Phoenix introducing the new "daily limit", which Nexus were keen to emphasise is "an experiment" they're open to feedback on. "We know that time in the New Mods view is important for a new mod to be discovered and we believe every mod author should have equal chances of having their work seen," they wrote. "While we're working on more sophisticated tools to give you control over the mods displayed to you, we are testing a stopgap solution that we hope will address the issue for now: For the time being, the New Mods view will display one mod per mod author. This limit refreshes every twenty-four hours – so if you publish one mod every day, you won't be affected."

The All Mods, Updated, Trending, Popular, and Surprise tabs for games are unaffected by the change, so will still dedicate a tab to each work regardless of who uploaded it when. If you take a glance at the New Mods pages for the likes of Skyrim, Fallout 4, and Cyberpunk 2077 this morning, you can already see the new mod stacking in action. The most mods from the same author I've seen stacked atop each other so far is 14 Fallout 4 works piled up.

It's worth noting you can also toggle the show only one new mod per modder rule off in the new mods tab, bringing back the older layout with one slot per mod regardless of uploader.

Personally, I tend to sort by mods with the most endorsements or downloads within the past 24 hours or seven days when I'm scanning for new mods, rather than just scrolling back through the new mods tab. Though I appreciate that could mean I've been missing out on some stellar works by lesser known modders whose creations never get the traction they merit thanks to being buried under an avalanche of other works. If so, hopefully this update does help the lone mods avoid being run over by mass upload freight trains.

#3923. Switch 2 and Switch consoles updated to version 23.5.0 as Nintendo quietly re-introduces eShop gifting

Nintendo has just pushed out a new update to all Switch and Switch 2 consoles, bringing the firmware on both up to version 23.5.0. The headline change with the new update is support and compatibility for an upcoming update that will allow members of a Nintendo Account family group to gift games to one another.

The feature itself is expected to go live on 17th November, 2026. "Just in time for the holidays, a new feature will let family group members gift digital games to other members of their group," says a post on a dedicated blog on the Nintendo site. "You will be able to gift digital products that you purchase through Nintendo eShop on your device to family group members. This includes eligible games as well as DLC and upgrade packs. As a reminder, anyone with a Nintendo Account can easily set up a family group and add members (up to 8 total)."

The publisher notes, however, that "some products may not be eligible for digital gifting" and that "supervised accounts are not able to send digital gifts". Additionally, "the number of digital gift purchases allowed in a given period is limited".

"This feature is a great way to celebrate a special occasion with your kids. Happy gifting!" concludes Nintendo. Just in time for the holidays, how thoughtful. It's worth noting that a previous iteration of this support was included back on the Nintendo Wii, but that was much more robust than this - back then, the publisher allowed users to send WiiWare or Virtual Console games to anyone on their Wii Friend list via the Wii Shop Channel, rather than just those limited to their immediate group. This functionality was lost in 2019, alongside the closure of the Wii Shop Channel.

The patch also came with some other updates, you can see those listed below.

Qud's co-creators discuss dogs with guns, handless tattooing, and the tragedy of a sinning tree.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In a GDC interview with Freehold Games in 2025, I asked the developers of magnificently mutated, indulgently arcane science-fantasy roguelike Caves of Qud the same thing anyone would in my situation: What's the ideal number of limbs for a being to aspire to? Their answer was none, because "a perfect sphere is the ideal form" and "we started in perfection and only moved farther from God."

As you can imagine, I was eager to speak with co-creators Brian Bucklew and Jason Grinblat earlier this month about Diaspora, the roguelike's upcoming first expansion. Diaspora aims to add an "influx of riotous life" to Qud, expanding its body plan-agnostic mutation system with playable animal and plant characters. With Qud's mutagenic possibility space about to erupt even further, I posed its developers another pressing question: Is it a greater moral tragedy for a sin to be committed by a man who mutated into a tree, or by a tree who mutated into a man?

"We have text on this in-game," Grinblat said, citing Aphorisms About Birds—an in-game book which notes that our fairy tales pay plenty of attention to the man who's turned into a bird, but little to the cruelty fate's inflicted on the bird who's turned into a man. "I think that's probably even more true if you're a tree. There's one tree mayor in the game. He's pretty happy. He's been around for a while. If he were a guy just walking around out there, getting acid gas shot at him, I think he'd be pretty upset."

"It hits too close to home, right? We're having trouble in our world dealing with things transforming into the facsimile of man," Bucklew said. "It's hard for me to think about turning into the facsimile of man without becoming sad about the way the world is and how real that question's going to be in our lives for the next 20 years."

Conversely, Grinblat noted, "becoming a tree sounds really nice." To that, Bucklew agreed, wondering whether "there's some way we can get into that business," possibly through marketing "some random peptide."

With an air of existential horror comfortably established, we moved into a more mechanical discussion of Diaspora's new plant and animal playstyles. In Caves of Qud, it's already possible for a player character to end up with all sorts of bodies: A mutant character could end up sprouting a bouquet of new limbs and body parts, each capable of equipping items and using abilities. And a number of the game's existing mutations allow a character to acquire some very animalian or plantlike characteristics, whether it's antlers, ape fur, or photosynthetic skin.

With Diaspora's plant and animal gene-stocks, however, the developers are aiming to lean even harder into exploring what more specialized body types provide—and what they don't.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

"They have different body plans. That's one that jumps out immediately," Grinblat said. "I'm a crab: I have six legs, I might have a claw. I'm a bear: I'm a quadruped that doesn't have hands in a traditional sense. That's already a space to play with."

That's elaborated on further with species traits, a new feature exclusive to Diaspora character types. Species traits are a kind of stock-specific mutation bonus, representing the inherent features of an animal's—or plant's—anatomy. While a human character can mutate wings, a mutant bird's inherent wing mutation will advance faster and allow access to new, bird-specific flight advancements. Same with tails: Mutant animal characters that possess a tail as a species trait will be able to mutate the appendage to be prehensile more quickly than mutant characters that don't.

"We want every animal to have something weird and unique about them that you can't just get if you were a human and you advance that mutation a bunch," Grinblat said.

Species traits will introduce a breadth of new opportunities for Qud's already-rich buildcrafting, but creating a new plant or animal character will mean opting out of some things that are standard to the human experience. For example: If I make a mutant dog, can I hold a gun without mutating new hands or opposable thumbs?

"This is a big thing. No," Grinblat said. "Right now, no."

There are, of course, ways for my mutant dog to achieve its dreams of weapon-wielding. I might seek out the helping hands artifact already present in-game, which provides the wearer with two extra arms and hands—or I could pick up that aforementioned prehensile tail mutation and grant my tail the gift of gunslinging. But while Grinblat acknowledged that "hands are very powerful," he said implementing those kinds of natural animal limitations are an intentional design decision, made in the hopes that players will explore new ways of surviving Qud's countless dangers.

"You might end up with a dog with a gun, but you might be doing a lot of dog stuff—running with a pack of dogs who each do their own thing," Grinblat said. "What an actual dog looks like in Qud is up for grabs, but we want to encourage different playstyles that animals can lean into without just feeling like, 'oh, I'm always going to get hands and use guns.'"

Unfortunately for Freehold, introducing a yet wider gradient of body types into the absurd complexity of Qud's systems and simulations has produced exciting new problems to solve—and philosophical riddles to ponder.

"We've spent so much time figuring out the ontology of tails," Bucklew said. "Are tails arms? Can they wear bracelets? How different is a prehensile tail from a regular tail? Is a tail different from a head in terms of what it can wear? A necklace? A bracelet? A lot of hours in meetings about tail ontology."

Freehold's "last three months," the Qud creators said, have been dominated by "people having strong opinions about limbs." Many of the emergent issues are related to Qud's core questline, which is requiring the devs to reevaluate all sorts of interactions that were designed under the assumption that the player would be roughly human-shaped.

"The limbs have taken the bulk of it, but there are other issues," Grinblat said. "Like, oh, I can't tattoo myself because I'm a crab, so I can't tattoo the Mark of Death on me. Or, oh, I can't eat because I'm a plant. I can't eat the Eater's Flesh that lets me advance past that part of the quest. There's all sorts of problems."

Crabs, in particular, seem to be a source of constant headache as Qud is reconfigured to accommodate animal playstyles.

"How does a crab get high? Like, it's an integral part of a Caves of Qud quest, and a crab is not very good at it," Bucklew said. "Do we need a tattooing booth? If you don't have hands, how are you going to tattoo yourself? We're going to need a tattoo grenade or something. But you can't throw stuff either. Oh man, I have no answer."

"God," Grinblat said. "It's so much to do."

By the end of our conversation, the developers remembered that crabs can probably hold a tattoo gun in their claws. Deciding how plants will tattoo themselves, they said, was a problem for another day.

Caves of Qud: Diaspora launches in early access on Steam on December 9.

#3921. Skydance Games lay off an undisclosed number of staff in the wake of Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, in latest case of consolidation killing livelihoods

A little over a month following the huge, vile, culture-defining (negative) merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. into Skydance, the corporation has confirmed that games division Skydance Games will be facing a round of layoffs, according to a report from Variety.

Skydance Games was born from combining Paramount and Warner Bros' own individual divisions, bringing developers like NetherRealm, Rocksteady, WB Games Montreal/Boston, TT Games and Avalanche under the same umbrella as Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra developers and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin publishers Paramount Games Studio. All this was was done, of course, to maximise the amount of IP that the corporation can access to base games on, such as Avatar: The Last Airbender, Game of Thrones, Star Trek, the DC Universe, Harry Potter, and more. Skydance Games came into existence on October 6th; it barely lasted a month as it was.

In a statement given to Variety, Skydance confirmed that "As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects. As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company." Skydance did not disclose the number of staff affected.

Skydance joins the ever-growing list of corporations that have mandated layoffs in the recent past, such as Microsoft, Ubisoft, and EA. Workers will bleed until there is no one left to cut. Solidarity to all affected.

#3920. Switch 2 US sales soar again thanks to The Legend of Zelda effect, as it enjoys its best week of the year so far

Could a remade Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time be exciting enough to revitalise Switch 2 hardware sales? That was the big question. And early sales figures suggest the answer is yes, it can.

The Switch 2, which had been declining in hardware sales over the last few months, just had its highest (dollar) sales week of 2026 in the US so far following the game's release, according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella on Bluesky.

The accompanying Legend of Zelda: 40th Anniversary Edition console in particular is responsible for a notable jump in Switch 2 hardware dollar sales. The themed, special edition console has been popular, with various retailers immediately running out of stock and a rise in scalping.

It's worth noting that The Legend of Zelda: 40th Anniversary Edition console, priced $520 / £430, does not include a copy of the game. Also, because the console was released 29th October, and the Ocarina of Time remake on 5th November, their sales results will come in separate monthly reports.

The Ocarina of Time launch also caused US hardware spending to jump by 81 percent during the week ending 31st October compared to the same period last year.

Christian Donlan awarded The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a glitzy five stars in Eurogamer's review, writing: "This is Ocarina as it's always been, as timeless and intricate, but it also has a vibrancy and clarity that makes it feel like it was just created last Wednesday."

If you're currently enjoying the remake, Eurogamer's Ocarina of Time walkthrough is a helpful companion with general tips, items and collectibles guide, quest walkthroughs and more.

On the eve of GTA 6 finally making its debut, it seems a lucky few have been given a special way to play it.

Several NBA players, all belonging to the Miami Heat team, have received a crazy care package from Rockstar Games that includes a special edition PS5 Pro console that's not publicly available.

Blade Runner 2099 isn't here just yet, with Amazon Prime's new take on the iconic cinematic cyberpunk universe set to arrive on November 25 – but its producers are already discussing a potential video game, apparently.

News of the possible game comes directly from IGN, who learns from Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson – Blade Runner 2099 executive producers and co-CEOs of Blade Runner franchise owner Alcon Entertainment – that, "yes," it might be underway somewhere down the line. And, furthermore, the two emphasize that it'll be a "AAA" project if anything, meaning this won't be a small fish situation… It may be the Blade Runner game.

Although Kosove and Johnson couldn't give much more information on the mysterious (possible, as it seems now) game, they do stress how important allowing players "interact" with the cyberpunk universe will be. It is, after all, a level of immersion Blade Runner's not really featured before, despite having been in the limelight in some shape or form since its 1982 debut film – the Ridley Scott classic that started it all.

I do wonder what the Blade Runner game might look like, should it come to fruition, though. Will it be akin to Cyberpunk 2077 – an RPG that leans heavily on player choice but builds its own universe with unique characters, standing comfortably separate from its tabletop source material – or shall it feature faces familiar to longtime fans (perhaps even those introduced in Blade Runner 2099 next week)? Only time will tell.

Regardless, it's an exciting time to be a fan of the gritty, sci-fi cyberpunk genre, if you ask me. Between CD Projekt Red's own confirmed Cyberpunk 2 and now a potential Blade Runner game, there's plenty for players to anticipate.
