#3917. Steam's new Steam Deck framerate graphs are good news for handheld players, though I wouldn't fully trust the numbers yet

Valve have finally made clear what they've been doing with all that hoovered-up performance data and all those "Framerate Estimator" text strings: a framerate estimator for the Steam Deck. Or, rather, a framerate average-r, as games on the Steam Store are now getting attached graphs – under their existing Steam Deck Compatibility details – that show how many frames-per-secondseses that game has been recording on real players' handhelds, the OLED and original LCD models both.

The thinking, as Valve explain in a Steam post, is to set more precise performance expectations than the existing verification ratings – Verified, Playable, and Unsupported – provide. This may induce some gentle learned nodding, if you've ever tried an Unsupported game only to find it works more or less fine, or have ever wondered why a game that can just about scrape 30fps together gets the same green good-job sticker as something that screams along at 90fps. Now, when checking that rating, you'll also get a relatively specific idea of smoothness and/or chugging potential.

Or will you? By Valve's own admission, the displayed results may be skewed by V-Sync treachery, where this anti-screen tear setting (which many games enable by default) could force games into briefly running at unrepresentative framerates. The scoundrel. My current handheld game beau, Mortal Shell II, looks like it may be falling victim to this: its results for the LCD Steam Deck show it mostly runs around 30fps, which is in line with my experience, but the OLED results show it averaging around 45fps. The Steam Deck OLED's APU is a tiny bit quicker than the LCD Deck's, but it's not that much of an upgrade.

There's work to be done, then, though I do appreciate the concept. As tightly as I cling to my battery-efficient, mercifully Windows-free Deck OLED in the face of drastically more powerful handhelds, with every year it becomes a little less likely that new games will comfortably run on it. Verification ratings can still act as decent (if broad) guidelines, but even with V-Sync putting an immaculately untorn thumb on the scales, game-specific framerate data will be much more illustrative.

As for whether these histograms will also get Steam Machine versions, or perhaps cover non-Valve handhelds, Valve say this: "We see this update as a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck. To this end, we are also prompting customers to opt-in to providing anonymized framerate data in the Steam desktop client. This opt-in is currently only on Steam Client Beta, and will ship to all customers in the future." So, maybe, if you gizzus yer data.

#3916. Under pressure, Big Walk studio reveals it used generative AI "sparingly" while making its hit 2026 game

"It has become a matter of public interest."

Australian developer House House has revealed it used generative AI "sparingly" to help make celebrated, indie, multiplayer puzzle game Big Walk.

In a statement sent to Aftermath - following a judging fallout related to the Independent Games Festival - House House revealed it had used large language models primarily to help debug the game's code.

"In the final stretch of Big Walk's development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs," the developer said. "In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code - we'd estimate that well under 0.1 percent of Big Walk's code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game."

House House added: "The primary use case for House House's use of LLMs was to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code."

The studio's revelation comes after a sizeable number of IGF jurors - 19 of them - issued a statement saying they would not vote for any game that used generative AI during its development. This was done after seeing "a significant increase" in entry submissions involving generative AI use, which "set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools". And rather than not vote for these in silence, a collection of jurors decided to take a public stand.

House House hadn't disclosed Big Walk generative AI use anywhere before disclosing it for its IGF submission. "We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage," the studio explained. "We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest."

House House added: "This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal. We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as 'inevitable'. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to video games and our world, and apologise that Big Walk's LLM usage may not meet their standards.

"Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards."

It's a revelation that's likely to leave a taint of some degree on one of this year's brightest stars - a game Eurogamer awarded a full five stars to in its Big Walk review.

If you're a World of Warcraft: Forever player you're almost certainly having your free time drained as you chain yourself to your desktop PC to play the game, or maybe a laptop. But for a small selection of true enthusiasts, the game is already working on mobile and handheld devices.

One such person showing off WoW: Forever on the go is none other than director of publishing at Larian, Michael Douse, who took to Twitter to show off the MMO being played on an AYN Thor device. For those who don't know, this is a fancy android handheld console, a sort of beefed up DS for the modern handheld aficionado.

"Arguably too many layers of abstraction," writes Douse. In the picture he posted, you can see the player character viewable on the Thor's top screen, while the map, text chat, skill UI, and buffs viewable on the bottom. It looks pretty cool, and is made possible due to JReese702's Github mod you can download at your leisure.

Arguably too many layers of abstraction pic.twitter.com/VjW0IX00Gg

But it's not the only mo-bell at the ball. Another Github WoW: Forever mod, WolkaraForever, gets the game playable on the iPhone Duo. As highlighted by CEO of esports company 100 Thieves Alex Wechsler on Twitter, the game looks to be ported pretty well to the phone, with mobile touchscreen controls viewable on both sides of the screen. Be warned though, as confirmed by Wechsler in a Twitter reply, it'll get your phone running hot.

As a father of 2 kids and always having wanted to play WOW, I’ve finally found a way 🥹 pic.twitter.com/eIVn0gn1WC

This coming alongside World of Warcraft: Forever's built-in (and very good) controller support could mean the game has real potential to spread far and wide across the vast array of different hardware out there. #3913. Tripwire Interactive says it's laying off 36 staff in a "necessary" decision, while reassuring that Killing Floor 3 and Maneater 2 are still in active development

In a statement posted yesterday, Killing Floor developers Tripwire Interactive have announced that the studio is laying off 36 "talented" internal staff as part of a "workforce reduction". The job cuts come 16 months after the release of Killing Floor 3 (which James didn't care for), and within hours of unrelated yet equally dispiriting redunancies at Skydance Games.

Tripwire's announcement claims that this was "not an easy decision, but unfortunately a necessary one for the organisation," adding that "these are truly great people who are exceptional at their roles, and we will help support these individuals with compassion and dignity during this transition." There's a small hope in me that this might mean helping those affected find new jobs quickly, though it's hard to stay optimistic when mass layoffs in games development have become such a regular occurrence.

Despite this post primarily being about the loss of 36 livelihoods, Tripwire are quick to reassure fans that Killing Floor 3's post-launch updates remain in active development, as does their comedy shark-action sequel Maneater 2. The studio "remain committed to our awesome community", they say; apparently just not to their awesome employees.

This news also arrives just days after Tripwire expanded its publishing business to support small indie developers, and less than a year after its last round of layoffs in March. Tripwire also happens to have been acquired by layoff extraordinaire corporation Embracer in 2022, just for some relevant context.

#3912. Round Up: GTA 6 Is Not Just the Most Acclaimed Game of 2026, It's the Highest-Rated Game of All Time

The initial reviews have arrived for GTA 6, and it's safe to say the game has been an absolute smash hit with critics.

The metascore has settled on a 99, making it one point off a "perfect" score of 100. In a year stuffed with fantastic games big and small, it's become the highest rated title of 2026.

More than that, though, it's the highest rated game of all time.

Review GTA 6 (PS5) - The Greatest Open World Game Ever Made

Reaching 99 is almost unheard of; only one other game has achieved the same level of acclaim — The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998).

However, GTA 6 has held onto its 99 score after more than 160 reviews; Ocarina of Time's metascore counts just 22 — though that's of course indicative of the era in which it released. There are simply more gaming outlets now, but that just means it's tougher to get consistent scores.

Rockstar's crime caper has received insanely consistent acclaim, and that might just give it an edge over the Nintendo classic. It's incredibly rare to see near-total agreement on a subjective work like this.

Critics are unanimous in their praise of GTA 6's open world, the relationship between protagonists Jason and Lucia, and the complex systems behind its myriad characters, activities, and missions.

Here are some snippets from just a few of the reviews — including our own, of course.

"GTA 6 is the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2. Rockstar has set a new sandbox standard here, with a world that feels alive and populated with real people; Leonida is a place where it appears almost anything can happen at any time."

"Somehow, GTA 6 lives up to the hype. Rockstar Games has crafted the most incredible open world I've ever experienced in a video game, packed with so much detail that I'll want to continue exploring it for months and likely years to come. It's coupled with a campaign that's full of extremely entertaining missions, led by two main characters who I've become much more invested in than I'd anticipated."

"Like all videogame protagonists, Jason and Lucia are ciphers through which the player exerts their will on the digital world. And yet, through the co-authored interplay of the characters Rockstar has written, and the people you personally tune them into becoming, they form one of the great partnerships in entertainment: beautiful and deadly, open to the possibilities of their world and, despite the violence they inflict on those beyond their circle, driven forward not by fear, but by love."

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that."

"Rockstar Games' latest release is a monumental achievement in storytelling, immersion, gameplay, and breadth of content."

"GTA 6 is the highest-fidelity sandbox of its generation. Rockstar has built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality. There's a degree of sophistication to everything GTA 6 does, and there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments."

"Only Rockstar commands the time and money necessary to make a game as dedicated to small details. And only Rockstar can execute on the realising such a granular vision unimpeachably. The obsession with the minutia both explains and justifies the 13-year wait. This game is the culmination of everything the developer has previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7."

"Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

"Grand Theft Auto 6 is a modern masterpiece. Rockstar's developers have created a remarkable open world that excels in storytelling, gameplay, visuals, music and technology to achieve something truly unmatched. Minor performance issues don’t dull the sparkle of an absolute must-play experience. GTA 6 was more than worth the wait."

Nintendo launches its official Black Friday Switch 2 deals this Sunday, November 22. But that doesn't mean there isn't already a wealth of discounts on the shelves. While things are a little slower in this department compared to PS5 (Sony dropped its own offers earlier this week), retailers like Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and GameStop have all launched their own early discounts and we're truly in the swing of sales now.

The big ticket we're waiting for is that Mario Kart World Switch 2 bundle. It's the go-to for anyone upgrading their handheld this Black Friday, packing a free copy of the latest racer as well as a Nintendo Switch Online Individual subscription. Considering the game itself usually piles an additional $79.99 onto your cart, that's a Black Friday deal to wait for.

You'll also be waiting until Sunday for $20 discounts on games like Donkey Kong Bananza and Kirby Air Riders, but plenty of third party titles or games not yet mentioned in Nintendo's upcoming Black Friday Switch 2 deals are already at their lowest prices yet. Ocarina of Time Remake, for example, has only just sailed down to its cheapest $54.99 rate this week, and you'll still find Mario Kart World on sale at Walmart by itself as well.

I've counted up 15 of the best Black Friday Nintendo Switch 2 deals you can already get your hands on before Ninty's sale has even begun - and you'll find them all just below.

I've spent more than seven years tracking Black Friday deals, but I watch prices on top games and gadgets all year round. I was with the Switch 2 from day one, completing GamesRadar+'s review of the latest generation handheld and going hands-on with as many accessories and titles as possible since. That means I know which prices actually represent discounts on the tech you actually need to know about.

The Nintendo Switch 2 is seeing a rare discount at Woot right now, with $30 off a new device. Savings here are usually limited to refurbished models so, while we're still above the previous $449 MSRP (prices jumped to $499 in November) this is one of the few discounts we've seen in the last couple of months.

Switch Sports Resort is being bundled in with the Nintendo Switch 2 console for just $30 extra right now. With the new $499 MSRP of the handheld and the latest island mini game pack coming in at $59.99, that's a solid saving.

This is Nintendo's Black Friday showpiece. The Mario Kart World bundle will be dropping to $499.99 from November 22, essentially netting you the $79.99 racer for free. That's with a Nintendo Switch Online Individual subscription thrown in as well.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has seen discounts in its life before, but only during its pre-order phase. That was when the physical edition dropped from $69.99 to $59.99. Today, the digital edition is giving us a brand new record-low price on 2026's biggest Ninty release.

Read more: Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time remake review

High on Life 2 is down to its lowest price yet in Amazon's Black Friday Nintendo Switch 2 deals. The FPS made its way to Ninty's handheld this year, but has been stuck at full price until July. Since then, it's only been on sale for about $40, before dropping down to today's $29.99 position.

So long as you don't mind adding a game-key card to your collection, Persona 3 Reload is down to just $25 right now ahead of Black Friday. This is a brand new record-low price on the Switch 2 version.

Mouse: PI for Hire is seeing its first ever discount right now, so while it may be small anyone waiting for a saving on this detective noir adventure should be taking notes. It's just started to move down the price scale to $34.99, so good things could be on their way.

Here's how this deal works. The Legend of Zelda Breath of the Wild will cost you $69 on Switch 2 if you buy the physical copy. An upgrade from the Switch 1 version, however, will only set you back $9.99. Take Woot's current $46.99 sale price on the original cart, add that upgrade price, and you've got the full Switch 2 experience for just $56.98 (about $12 off).

Read more: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild review

Metroid Ravenous is seeing the same pattern a number of first party Switch 2 pre-orders have seen this year - a $10 discount at Amazon that disappears after release. This is a solid chance to save ahead of that January launch date.

We've only ever seen Pokemon Scarlet drop to $45 once in the many years since its original release date. So, while this is an older Switch title, it runs great on Switch 2 and this is definitely a rare discount if you've not played it yet.

Mario Kart World still retails for essentially full price, which was $79 on launch day. Seeing any kind of discount on this racer is pretty rare, but Walmart's early Black Friday deals have it down to $68.40 now.

Donkey Kong Bananza will be $49.99 when Nintendo unleashes its full Black Friday sale on November 22. That will represent a record-low on the rarely discounted bananza smasher.

Kirby Air Riders will drop down to $39.99 on November 22, another record-low for a game that's seen a little more wiggle room on its price tag compared to Donkey Kong. Air Riders has shifted between $50 and $60 for a few months now, but it's never dropped this cheap.

Metroid Prime 4 will be another Switch 2 game joining the $39.99 club this Black Friday. We're already half way there at Amazon, but it's worth holding off on this one until November 22.

It may be an OG Switch port of two far older games, but the Super Mario Galaxy collection doesn't see too many discounts day to day. This one's only dropped to a similar $48.97 position once before Black Friday, back in September.

The Switch 2 version of Super Mario Party Jamboree is actually one of the most expensive games on the system, but the full cart has dropped to this Black Friday's $59.99 price before. That was during a very brief flash sale back in March, though, otherwise this is an $80 title day to day.

The PowerA Slim Case is one of the cheaper clamshell options on the market, so its $19.99 MSRP doesn't have too far to drop. A 25% discount takes a solid $5 off the price here, within a few pennies of its lowest ever.

The Turtle Beach Airlite Fit is one of the cheapest headset options out there for the Switch 2 at full price, so a record-low $14.99 is going to be particularly handy for anyone looking for an easy wired set of cups.

Featured in: Best Nintendo Switch headset

Read more: Turtle Beach Airlite Fit review

A smaller saving on a cheaper Joy-Con replacement system here. The GameSir X5s doesn't hold up against some of the more luxurious options on the market, but if you want a wider set of gamepads for handheld mode it's looking far more affordable than official pads right now.

The GameSir Super Nova regularly tails it down to this $29.99 sales position, but that doesn't make it any less impressive. In the hands this feels far more premium than a $30 gamepad should. Considering we're at a record-low price and this is the rate I'd expect to see in official Black Friday Nintendo Switch 2 deals, this is an easy win.

Featured in: Best Nintendo Switch 2 controllers

A golden oldie here, the Razer Barracuda X has been a go-to Switch headset for almost as long as it's been on the shelves, and it rarely drops below today's $69 sales position.

Black Friday itself officially kicks off on November 27, but Nintendo's offers come into full effect on November 22. That's for physical games and handhelds, though. Digital collectors are also being treated to an eShop sale running from November 19 until December 2.

We're also busy preparing for this year's best Black Friday PS5 deals and the best Black Friday gaming laptop deals as well.

#3910. "A fight for all workers": SAG-AFTRA throw weight behind emerging Rockstar union ahead of its GTA 6 release week vote

In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies."

If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important leverage from a global force.

SAG-AFTRA's statement declares that "unionisation is vital for the future of the video game industry", and that "in the face of record layoffs, job instability, hostile work places, and toxic crunch culture, it is now more critical than ever for unions and workers to stand in support of one another." They advocate for fair treatment, especially in the wake of displacement due to corporate mismanagement and genAI, and proudly state that "this is a fight for all workers."

Their statement closes by saying that "the gaming industry is a commercial juggernaut, and the people that create these amazing works of art deserve fair treatment and the opportunity to improve the terms of their employment with a strong voice at the bargaining table. We honor the courage of our fellow game workers at Rockstar and proudly support their union vote."

Solidarity with the workers, always. We can only wait and see how the voting process pans out.

#3909. As Arc Raiders celebrates its first birthday, publisher Nexon reveals the extraction shooter has topped 17 million sales, but revenue is set to decline

Arc Raiders, Embark Studios' popular extraction shooter, has exceeded 17m copies sold, according to publisher Nexon.

Arc Raiders was released at the end of October 2025, so reaching that milestone in a year is nothing to scoff at. According to Nexon's latest earnings report, however, only 1m copies of those 17 were sold in the third quarter - meaning sales have certainly slowed down.

Relatedly, Nexon said it expects Arc Raiders' revenue to decline in the fourth quarter compared to the same period last year - when the game enjoyed its hugely successful launch - and anticipates revenue will be "broadly flat sequentially". Despite this, the company said Arc Raiders' revenue was "within the outlook", naming its Frozen Trail update as a key moment that brought back some lapsed players while introducing new ones.

Indeed, Frozen Trail boosted the game's Steam player count, and reports suggest it also helped Arc Raiders hit a six-month player high across various platforms.

Even with its slowing sales, Arc Raiders remains one of Nexon's most successful titles. The company primarily attributed an overall year-on-year revenue increase, for the nine months ended 30th September, to the game.

Looking ahead, the biggest question hanging over Arc Raiders is whether or not it's going to get a dedicated PvE playlist. Following a successful test earlier this summer, Embark has been coy, and hasn't said whether PvE will return as a permanent feature. Arc Raiders' Chinese version does have a dedicated PvE mode, and executive producer Aleksander Grøndal said he could see both PvP and PvE modes co-existing in the future.

Consoles cost more than ever, and even if you can afford to buy one you don't have as much left over to buy games for it as you used to. That's made 2026 an underwhelming year for console gaming sales, but according to the latest forecast from videogame market analysts Newzoo, the imminent launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will turn that around.

"As we explored in the Global Games Market Report 2026," said Newzoo's director of market intelligence, Emmanuel Rosier, "without GTA VI the console market would likely be down year-over-year in 2026. Instead, the game's launch is expected to generate billions of dollars in revenue and give console spending a significant boost."

Rosier is the analyst who, back in August, was skeptical about the idea of BioWare surviving long enough to make another Mass Effect game. I wish he'd been wrong about that, but it turned out he was right on the money with that prediction.

"Western console has been losing ground," he went on to say. "Its share of global games revenue fell from 21.5% in 2015 to 17.1% in 2025, and its revenue has been broadly flat since 2021. Console adoption shows the same pattern. In Western markets, the console player base has been flat since 2022. Most people who want to play on console already do."

Newzoo's prediction is that GTA 6 "will lift console full-game spending by 17.5% this year". But that's just the start of the story. "So while GTA VI is undoubtedly one of the most important releases of the decade," Rosier says, "its initial impact will be concentrated in Western console. That’s still a big market, which we forecast will be worth $36.3 billion in 2026, but it's only part of the industry. The longer-term global story will depend on what happens next, particularly on PC and online."

Though tradition has plenty of people expecting a delay of roughly a year and a half between GTA 6's console and PC releases, general console malaise and the value of GTA Online—likely to be bigger on PC, and perhaps launch alongside the PC port—is a reason to think maybe the wait won't be so long. A recent GamesBeat report claims it'll be out in early 2027.

"PC is far bigger than console in several major markets, including China," Rosier says, "and a PC release could expose the game to a much broader international audience.

"The online mode is another key unknown. Depending on how it's positioned and monetized, it could significantly expand the game's audience. If Rockstar adopts a model that lowers barriers to entry, the long-term opportunity outside the traditional Western console audience could be much larger than it appears today."

GTA Online was a huge part of GTA 5's long-tail success. While Newzoo's data says at least 37% of players who preordered GTA 6 have spent money on GTA Online, only 15% did so in the last 12 months. It's in need of a refresh, and though Rockstar haven't confirmed anything, Twitch's CEO also says GTA 6's multiplayer component will be out in 2027.
